1.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Meals and entertainment

**FAQ-13. Can I grab a bite while I am away on a work trip, and how much can I spend?**

Yes, during a business trip. A business trip is travel more than 50 km from your usual office, approved by your manager. Meals are reimbursed at actual cost up to EUR 15 for breakfast, EUR 25 for lunch and EUR 45 for dinner. These limits apply to your own meal only. (Expense Policy 2.1, Definitions)

Employee Expenses FAQ: Meals and entertainment

**FAQ-15. How much can I spend when I take a client out for a meal?**

Up to EUR 80 per attendee, and every attendee counts, including Larkfield employees. For example, a lunch with two clients costing EUR 210 for three people is within the limit when the attendee list is provided. The claim must also give the business purpose of the meeting. (Expense Policy 2.2, Appendix A)

Expense Policy: 2. Meals

**2.1 Meals during business trips.** During a business trip, Larkfield reimburses meals at their actual cost up to these limits per meal: breakfast EUR 15, lunch EUR 25, dinner EUR 45. Limits apply to the employee's own meal. Meals on days without travel are not reimbursed unless clause 2.2 or 2.4 applies.

2.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Meals and entertainment

**FAQ-20. Can we have wine at a client dinner?**

Yes, alcohol is allowed as part of client entertainment. It must stay within the EUR 80 per attendee limit, together with the food and everything else on the bill. As always for client entertainment, the claim needs the attendee list and the business purpose. (Expense Policy 2.2, 2.3)

Employee Expenses FAQ: Meals and entertainment

**FAQ-19. Can I put a beer with my dinner on my trip expenses?**

Not when you ate without clients. Alcohol is reimbursed only as part of client entertainment. The policy does not say how to handle one receipt that has both food and alcohol on it. A claim that exceeds a rule is rejected as a whole, and mixed receipts are rejected too, so ask Finance how to submit it before you upload. (Expense Policy 2.3, 7.1, 7.4)

Expense Policy: 2. Meals

**2.3 Alcohol.** Alcohol is reimbursed only as part of client entertainment under clause 2.2, and within its per-attendee limit. Alcohol on a business trip meal without clients is not reimbursed.

4.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Travel

**FAQ-29. Can I go first class on the train?**

Rail travel is booked in second class. First class is allowed for a single journey longer than 4 hours. A trip made of two shorter journeys does not qualify just because the total is long, because the rule is about a single journey. (Expense Policy 3.2)

Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**3.2 Rail travel.** Rail travel is booked in second class. First class is allowed for a single journey longer than 4 hours.

Contractor Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**C3.2 Rail travel.** Rail travel is booked in second class only. First class is not reimbursed, including on long journeys. When only first class is available on a service, the contractor chooses a different service or explains the case to the engagement manager before booking.

5.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Travel

**FAQ-23. Can I take a taxi home after a late client dinner?**

Yes, when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00, because public transport is then not treated as a reasonable option. The limit is EUR 60 per trip. The dinner itself is a separate claim that needs its own attendee list. Keep the taxi receipt, because it shows the time the trip started. (Expense Policy 3.3, 2.2)

Employee Expenses FAQ: Travel

**FAQ-24. Can I take a cab to a client meeting at 2 in the afternoon?**

Only if public transport is not a reasonable option. The policy names three cases: you are carrying equipment, no public transport runs, or the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. A EUR 22 cab at 14:00 with no equipment is not covered unless public transport does not run. The limit is EUR 60 per trip. (Expense Policy 3.3, Appendix A)

Employee Expenses FAQ: Travel

**FAQ-25. My cab from the airport in London cost more than the usual cab limit. Is that allowed?**

It can be. The usual limit is EUR 60 per trip. An airport transfer in a high-cost city may exceed it when the receipt shows the airport as the start or end of the trip. London is a high-cost city, along with Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York and Oslo. The policy does not give a higher figure, so ask Finance if the fare is large. (Expense Policy 3.3, Definitions)

6.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Hotels

**FAQ-32. What is the most I can spend on a hotel room?**

EUR 150 per night, or EUR 220 per night in a high-cost city: London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York or Oslo. For example, a night in a Paris hotel at EUR 205 is within the limit. A claim over the limit is rejected as a whole, and you submit it again with an amount within the limit. (Expense Policy 3.5, 7.1, Appendix A)

Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**3.5 Hotels.** Hotel rooms are reimbursed up to EUR 150 per night, or EUR 220 per night in a high-cost city. The limit covers the room and breakfast when breakfast is included in the rate. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit.

Contractor Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**C3.5 Hotels.** Hotel rooms are reimbursed up to EUR 130 per night, or EUR 190 per night in a high-cost city. The limit covers the room and breakfast when breakfast is included in the rate. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit.

7.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Hotels

**FAQ-34. Can I claim the minibar or a film I watched in my room?**

No. Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. If these are on the same hotel bill as the room, the bill is a mixed receipt: the claim is rejected, and you submit it again without the personal items. (Expense Policy 3.6, 7.4)

Contractor Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**C3.6 Hotel extras.** Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. Laundry is reimbursed only on trips of 5 nights or longer. A hotel bill that mixes the room with these extras is handled under clause C8.4.

Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**3.6 Hotel extras.** Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. Laundry is reimbursed only on trips of 5 nights or longer.

8.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Submitting a claim

**FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?**

Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2)

Employee Expenses FAQ: Receipts

**FAQ-8. I lost the receipt. Can I still claim?**

Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice, and the policy has no rule that replaces a lost one. If you still have the payment card slip and the amount is EUR 25 or less, the slip is accepted. Above EUR 25 you must provide the itemised receipt. The policy does not say whether a bank or card statement can stand in, so ask Finance before you submit. (Expense Policy 1.3)

Employee Expenses FAQ: Receipts

**FAQ-10. What does a receipt actually have to show?**

It must show the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, and the total. If tax was charged, the tax amount must be shown too. A receipt that shows only a total is not enough, except for the card slip case up to EUR 25. Check for these details before you leave the shop or close the booking page. (Expense Policy 1.3)

9.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Equipment and software

**FAQ-37. Can I buy a new laptop or phone myself?**

Laptops and phones are supplied by IT. If you buy one yourself, it needs a pre-approval reference at any price. Get the reference from Finance before the purchase. IT supplies the device, so ask IT first. (Expense Policy 4.1)

IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 2. Requesting additional equipment through the IT portal

**IT2.5 Laptops and phones are not bought personally.** IT supplies laptops and phones, and employees do not buy them. If an employee buys one personally, Finance can reimburse it only when a pre-approval reference was issued before the purchase, at any price (Expense Policy clause 4.1). This is allowed only in exceptional cases, for example when a laptop is lost during travel and IT cannot deliver a replacement in time.

IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 4. Home-office equipment

**IT4.3 Items above EUR 300.** An item above EUR 300 needs a pre-approval reference issued before the purchase. The employee requests it as described in section 3 and attaches the product page or quote. If the employee buys such an item without a reference, Finance cannot reimburse it.

10.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Equipment and software

**FAQ-38. I paid for a software subscription that I use for work. Can I claim it?**

No. Software and subscriptions are bought by IT through the company account, so licences can be managed and cancelled. Software bought personally is not reimbursed, even when you use it for work. If you need a tool, ask IT to buy it. (Expense Policy 4.2)

IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 5. Software and subscriptions

**IT5.2 Why personal purchases are not reimbursed.** Software bought personally is not reimbursed, even when it is used for work (Expense Policy clause 4.2). IT cannot see, renew, move or cancel a personal licence, and it cannot check the vendor's data protection terms. A subscription that nobody at Larkfield owns also continues to charge after the employee leaves.

Expense Policy: 4. Equipment and software

**4.2 Software.** Software and subscriptions are bought by IT through the company account so licences can be managed and cancelled. Software bought personally is not reimbursed, even when it is used for work.

11.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: What is never reimbursed

**FAQ-43. I got a parking ticket on a business trip. Can I claim it?**

No. Parking tickets, speeding fines and other penalties are never reimbursed, even when incurred on a business trip. This holds even if a tight meeting schedule caused the ticket. (Expense Policy 6.1)

Expense Policy: 6. Not reimbursed

**6.1 Fines.** Parking tickets, speeding fines, and other penalties are never reimbursed, even when incurred on a business trip.

Expense Policy: 1. General rules

**1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. An expense is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose.

A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. For anything above EUR 25 you need the itemised receipt or invoice. If the shop can print or email an itemised copy, ask for it at the till, because it is the safer document to upload. (Expense Policy 1.3)

13.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Travel

**FAQ-30. I drove my own car to a client site. What can I claim?**

Private car use is reimbursed at EUR 0.30 per kilometre. In the claim, state the start address, the end address and the distance. Fuel receipts are not reimbursed separately when you claim mileage, so do not upload a petrol receipt for the same drive. (Expense Policy 3.4)

Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**3.4 Private car.** Use of a private car is reimbursed at EUR 0.30 per kilometre. The claim states the start and end address and the distance. Fuel receipts are not reimbursed separately when mileage is claimed.

Employee Expenses FAQ: Using the intake desk

**FAQ-54. Can I upload several receipts from one trip as a single claim?**

A claim is one receipt or invoice with its information, so each receipt is its own claim. The policy does not describe bundling several receipts into one upload, so ask Finance if you want to try. Each claim states its own business purpose, which is also what separates genuine look-alike purchases from duplicates. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.4, 1.5)

14.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Training

**FAQ-40. Can I expense a book or an online course for my job?**

Yes. Books, online courses and certification exams related to your role are reimbursed up to EUR 500 per calendar year. A claim that goes over a limit is rejected as a whole. The policy does not describe how Finance tracks your yearly total, so ask Finance if you are unsure how much you have left. (Expense Policy 5.1, 7.1)

Expense Policy: 5. Training and books

**5.1 Books and courses.** Books, online courses and certification exams related to the employee's role are reimbursed up to EUR 500 per calendar year.

Contractor Expense Policy: 5. Training and conferences

**C5.1 Books and courses.** Books, online courses and certification exams are not reimbursed to contractors, unless the statement of work says so. A statement of work that allows training names the amount or the course. Without that wording, the cost is the contractor's own investment in their skills.

15.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Decisions and appeals

**FAQ-50. Can Finance just pay the part that is within the limit?**

No. Finance does not part-approve claims, so that every booked amount matches a document. A claim over a limit is rejected as a whole, and you submit it again with the amount within the limit. (Expense Policy 7.1)

Expense Policy: 7. Decisions

**7.1 Limits.** A claim that exceeds a limit in this policy is rejected as a whole. The employee may submit it again with the amount within the limit, explaining the difference in the business purpose. Finance does not part-approve claims, so that every booked amount matches a document.

Employee Expenses FAQ: Decisions and appeals

**FAQ-49. My claim was rejected because it was over a limit. What now?**

Submit it again with the amount within the limit, and explain the difference in the business purpose. For example, a EUR 52 dinner on a trip is over the EUR 45 dinner limit and is rejected, while a claim for EUR 45 with a note is accepted. The policy describes no separate appeal. If you think the decision was wrong, ask Finance. The policy does not say that a new submission restarts the 60-day deadline, so do not wait. (Expense Policy 7.1, 1.2, Appendix A)

16.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Hotels

**FAQ-33. Does the hotel breakfast count toward the limit? And the city tax?**

When breakfast is included in the room rate, the limit covers the room and the breakfast together. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit, so they do not count toward it. The policy does not cover a hotel that bills breakfast as a separate item, so ask Finance in that case. (Expense Policy 3.5)

Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**3.5 Hotels.** Hotel rooms are reimbursed up to EUR 150 per night, or EUR 220 per night in a high-cost city. The limit covers the room and breakfast when breakfast is included in the rate. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit.

Contractor Expense Policy: 3. Travel

**C3.5 Hotels.** Hotel rooms are reimbursed up to EUR 130 per night, or EUR 190 per night in a high-cost city. The limit covers the room and breakfast when breakfast is included in the rate. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit.

17.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: What is never reimbursed

**FAQ-44. Can I expense a leaving present for a colleague, or a gift for a client?**

A gift for a colleague is a personal expense. The policy says nothing about gifts for clients, so ask Finance before you buy one. Gift cards and vouchers are not reimbursed whoever they are for. (Expense Policy 6.2, 6.3)

Employee Expenses FAQ: What is never reimbursed

**FAQ-45. Can I put a prepaid card or a shop voucher on my claim?**

No. Gift cards, vouchers and prepaid cards are not reimbursed, because they cannot be matched to a business expense. If you bought something real with the voucher, the policy does not cover that purchase through the voucher, so ask Finance. (Expense Policy 6.3)

Expense Policy: 6. Not reimbursed

**6.3 Vouchers.** Gift cards, vouchers and prepaid cards are not reimbursed, because they cannot be matched to a business expense.

18.text:
IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 3. Pre-approval references

**IT3.1 What a reference is.** A pre-approval reference is an identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN`, for example `PA-2026-014`. Finance issues it before the purchase, and it shows that the purchase and its budget were agreed in advance. YYYY is the year in which the reference was issued and NNN is a running number within that year.

IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 3. Pre-approval references

**IT3.3 Who approves.** The employee's manager first confirms the business need in the portal. A Finance reviewer then checks the budget and issues the reference, normally within 3 working days of the manager's approval. IT does not issue references; it forwards the request to Finance.

IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 3. Pre-approval references

**IT3.4 Validity of 90 days.** A reference is valid for 90 days from the day it is issued, and the purchase must be made inside that period. A reference covers one purchase. If the purchase is not made in time, the employee requests a new reference; Finance does not extend an old one. The 90 days limit when the purchase is made. They do not change the 60-day claim deadline in Expense Policy clause 1.2, which runs from the document date.

22.text:
Employee Expenses FAQ: Decisions and appeals

**FAQ-52. How long does Finance take to review a claim?**

Finance aims for 5 working days. The policy itself sets no review time. If the reviewer asks you for information, the claim continues once you answer, so a quick answer keeps it moving. (Expense Policy 7.2)

Expense Policy: 1. General rules

**1.2 Submission deadline.** A claim must be submitted within 60 days of the document date. Claims submitted later are rejected. The deadline exists because Finance closes each quarter's accounts and late claims cannot be booked to the right period.

Employee Expenses FAQ: Submitting a claim

**FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?**

You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2)

Free software is still software for the purposes of this policy, and a tool is not exempt from review because it costs nothing.

25.text:
IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 7. Loss, theft and damage

**IT7.1 Report within 24 hours.** An employee reports a lost or stolen device, or a suspected leak of credentials, to IT within 24 hours of noticing it. The report is made in the IT portal, or by telephone to the IT service desk when the portal is not reachable. The 24 hours run from when the employee noticed, but employees should not wait.

IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 7. Loss, theft and damage

**IT7.4 Replacement.** IT replaces a lost, stolen or irreparably damaged device from stock, or orders a new one, after the manager confirms the circumstances. A replacement does not restart the replacement cycle in clause IT1.6, so a laptop that is lost in its second year is replaced and is still due for renewal in year 3 of the original issue. Larkfield does not deduct the cost of a device from salary.

IT Equipment and Procurement Policy: 7. Loss, theft and damage

**IT7.2 What IT does.** On receiving the report IT locks the device and revokes its sessions, and it wipes the device if it is not recovered within 48 hours. For a theft, the employee also reports it to the police where it happened and gives IT the police reference number. IT keeps the report in the equipment record.

You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. **IT7.1 Report within 24 hours.** An employee reports a lost or stolen device, or a suspected leak of credentials, to IT within 24 hours of noticing it. Pre-approval references **IT3.1 What a reference is.** A pre-approval reference is an identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN`, for example `PA-2026-014`. Finance issues it before the purchase, and it shows that the purchase and its budget were agreed in advance. YYYY is the year in which the reference was issued and NNN is a running number within that year. **IT3.2 Requesting a reference.** The employee requests a reference in the IT portal, under "Request pre-approval". The request names the item or event, the supplier or venue, the expected cost in euros, the date of the purchase, and the business purpose. (Expense Policy 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, Definitions) **FAQ-15. How much can I spend when I take a client out for a meal?** Up to EUR 80 per attendee, and every attendee counts, including Larkfield employees. For example, a lunch with two clients costing EUR 210 for three people is within the limit when the attendee list is provided. The claim must also give the business purpose of the meeting. (Expense Policy 2.2, Appendix A) **FAQ-16. I took a client to dinner but did not write down who came. Is that a problem?** Yes. A client entertainment claim must list the names and companies of all attendees, and without the list it cannot be assessed against the limit. This is information you can still provide, so the reviewer asks you for it instead of rejecting the claim. The claim continues once you answer. (Expense Policy 2.2, 7.2) **FAQ-17. Can my partner's dinner go on the claim?** The policy does not mention spouses, partners or other personal guests. Trip meals cover your own meal only, and a client entertainment claim lists the names and companies of the attendees you met for work. Every claim also needs a business purpose. Ask Finance before you include anyone who was not there for a work reason. (Expense Policy 1.5, 2.1, 2.2) **FAQ-18. We split the bill at dinner with colleagues. Who claims it?** The policy has no rule about splitting a bill. It does say the same expense may be claimed only once, so two people should not both claim the same receipt. For client entertainment, one claim lists all attendees. Ask Finance how to submit a split bill before you upload it. (Expense Policy 1.4, 2.1, 2.2) **FAQ-19. Can I put a beer with my dinner on my trip expenses?** Not when you ate without clients. Alcohol is reimbursed only as part of client entertainment. The policy does not say how to handle one receipt that has both food and alcohol on it.

4.text: Meals on days without travel are not reimbursed unless clause 2.2 or 2.4 applies. **2.2 Client entertainment.** A meal with clients or partners is reimbursed up to EUR 80 per attendee, counting every attendee including Larkfield employees. The claim must list the names and companies of all attendees and the business purpose of the meeting. A client entertainment claim without the attendee list cannot be assessed against the limit. **2.3 Alcohol.** Alcohol is reimbursed only as part of client entertainment under clause 2.2, and within its per-attendee limit. Alcohol on a business trip meal without clients is not reimbursed. **2.4 Team meals.** A meal for a Larkfield team (no clients) is reimbursed only with a pre-approval reference. Team meals are usually celebrations or offsites that managers plan in advance; the reference confirms the budget was agreed. **2.5 Tips.** Tips are reimbursed up to 10% of the bill before the tip. Any tip above 10% is a personal expense. ## 3. Travel **3.1 Air travel.** Flights are booked in economy class. Premium economy is allowed for flights over 6 hours. Business and first class are not reimbursed. Flights should be booked at least 14 days before departure; a later booking is allowed when the trip itself was arranged at short notice, and the business purpose says so. **3.2 Rail travel.** Rail travel is booked in second class. First class is allowed for a single journey longer than 4 hours. **3.3 Taxis and ride-hailing.** A taxi or ride-hailing trip is reimbursed when public transport is not a reasonable option: when carrying equipment, when no public transport runs, or when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. The limit is EUR 60 per trip. Airport transfers in a high-cost city may exceed this limit when the receipt shows the airport as start or end of the trip. **3.4 Private car.** Use of a private car is reimbursed at EUR 0.30 per kilometre. The claim states the start and end address and the distance. Fuel receipts are not reimbursed separately when mileage is claimed. **3.5 Hotels.** Hotel rooms are reimbursed up to EUR 150 per night, or EUR 220 per night in a high-cost city. The limit covers the room and breakfast when breakfast is included in the rate. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit. **3.6 Hotel extras.** Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. Laundry is reimbursed only on trips of 5 nights or longer. ## 4.

**C2.4 Team meals.** Meals with a Larkfield team, such as celebrations or offsites, are not reimbursed to contractors. When the engagement manager invites a contractor to such an event, Larkfield pays for the event directly. The contractor does not pay and claim the cost, so that the event budget stays with the manager who planned it. **C2.5 Tips.** Tips are reimbursed up to 5% of the bill before the tip. Any tip above 5% is a personal expense. The tip must appear on the receipt or card slip so the reviewer can check the percentage. **C2.6 Meals included in other costs.** A meal that is already paid through another cost is not invoiced a second time. This covers breakfast included in the hotel rate, meals served on a flight or train, and meals provided at a client site. When a contractor skips a meal that was included, no allowance is paid in its place, because this policy reimburses actual costs only. ## 3. Travel **C3.1 Air travel.** Flights are booked in economy class only, regardless of the length of the flight. Premium economy, business and first class are not reimbursed. Flights should be booked at least 14 days before departure; a later booking is allowed when the engagement manager asked for the trip at short notice, and the business purpose says so. **C3.2 Rail travel.** Rail travel is booked in second class only. First class is not reimbursed, including on long journeys. When only first class is available on a service, the contractor chooses a different service or explains the case to the engagement manager before booking. **C3.3 Taxis and ride-hailing.** A taxi or ride-hailing trip is reimbursed when public transport is not a reasonable option: when carrying work equipment, when no public transport runs, or when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. The limit is EUR 40 per trip. The limit applies to every trip, including airport transfers in a high-cost city. **C3.4 Private car.** Use of a private car is reimbursed at EUR 0.25 per kilometre. The expense line states the start and end address and the distance. Fuel receipts are not reimbursed separately when mileage is claimed, because the mileage rate already covers fuel. **C3.5 Hotels.** Hotel rooms are reimbursed up to EUR 130 per night, or EUR 190 per night in a high-cost city. The limit covers the room and breakfast when breakfast is included in the rate. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit. **C3.6 Hotel extras.** Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. Laundry is reimbursed only on trips of 5 nights or longer.

The usual limit is EUR 60 per trip. An airport transfer in a high-cost city may exceed it when the receipt shows the airport as the start or end of the trip. London is a high-cost city, along with Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York and Oslo. The policy does not give a higher figure, so ask Finance if the fare is large. (Expense Policy 3.3, Definitions) **FAQ-26. Can I upgrade to business class on a long flight?** No. Business and first class are not reimbursed. Flights are booked in economy, and premium economy is allowed for flights over 6 hours. On a shorter flight, premium economy is not covered either. If you pay for an upgrade yourself, it is your own cost. (Expense Policy 3.1) **FAQ-27. The trip came up at the last minute, so I booked my flight only a few days ahead. Will that be refused?** Flights should be booked at least 14 days before departure. A later booking is allowed when the trip itself was arranged at short notice, and your business purpose must say so. Write that in the claim. (Expense Policy 3.1, 1.5) **FAQ-28. My flight got cancelled and I had to buy a new ticket. Is that covered?** The policy has no rule for cancelled flights. The normal flight rules still apply: economy, or premium economy over 6 hours. A booking less than 14 days ahead is allowed when the trip was arranged at short notice, and the business purpose must say so. Explain what happened in the business purpose and ask Finance how to claim the new ticket. (Expense Policy 3.1, 1.5) **FAQ-29. Can I go first class on the train?** Rail travel is booked in second class. First class is allowed for a single journey longer than 4 hours. A trip made of two shorter journeys does not qualify just because the total is long, because the rule is about a single journey. (Expense Policy 3.2) **FAQ-30. I drove my own car to a client site. What can I claim?** Private car use is reimbursed at EUR 0.30 per kilometre. In the claim, state the start address, the end address and the distance. Fuel receipts are not reimbursed separately when you claim mileage, so do not upload a petrol receipt for the same drive. (Expense Policy 3.4) **FAQ-31. Can I rent a car for a client visit?** The policy does not mention rental cars. It covers the use of your own private car at EUR 0.30 per kilometre, and the general rule is that a cost must be reasonable for your role and purpose. Ask Finance before you book a rental so you know it will be accepted.

Can I take a taxi home after a late client dinner?** Yes, when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00, because public transport is then not treated as a reasonable option. The limit is EUR 60 per trip. The dinner itself is a separate claim that needs its own attendee list. Keep the taxi receipt, because it shows the time the trip started. (Expense Policy 3.3, 2.2) **FAQ-24. Can I take a cab to a client meeting at 2 in the afternoon?** Only if public transport is not a reasonable option. The policy names three cases: you are carrying equipment, no public transport runs, or the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. A EUR 22 cab at 14:00 with no equipment is not covered unless public transport does not run. The limit is EUR 60 per trip. (Expense Policy 3.3, Appendix A) **FAQ-25. My cab from the airport in London cost more than the usual cab limit. Is that allowed?** It can be. The usual limit is EUR 60 per trip.

8.text: ## Submitting a claim **FAQ-1. How do I get back money I paid out of my own pocket for work?** Submit a claim with the receipt and one sentence saying what the spend was for. Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job, and "employee" includes anyone on the payroll, even during probation. A cost is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5) **FAQ-2. Is it enough to write "work stuff" as the reason for the expense?** No. Write one sentence that says what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" on its own is not accepted as a business purpose. A good example is "Dinner with the client team during the Hamburg trip", because a reviewer can read it and know what the money bought. (Expense Policy 1.5) **FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?** You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?** Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-5. I uploaded the same receipt twice by mistake. Is that a problem?** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. Your first claim is not affected by this. You do not need to do anything about the first one. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-6. I really did buy two identical things at the same shop on the same day. Will the system think I cheated?** Two claims with the same vendor, total and document date look like duplicates, and the later one is rejected. If the two purchases were genuine, say so in the business purpose of the claim. That explanation is how the reviewer can tell the two claims apart. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-7. I am not sure whether something is allowed. Who do I ask?** Ask Finance, which owns the policy.

Who do I ask?** Ask Finance, which owns the policy. Ask before you buy, because a pre-approval reference is issued before the purchase, and the policy has no way to get one afterwards. If the policy is silent on your situation, Finance is the team that answers. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1) ## Receipts **FAQ-8. I lost the receipt. Can I still claim?** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice, and the policy has no rule that replaces a lost one. If you still have the payment card slip and the amount is EUR 25 or less, the slip is accepted. Above EUR 25 you must provide the itemised receipt. The policy does not say whether a bank or card statement can stand in, so ask Finance before you submit. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-9. The shop only gave me the slip from the card machine. Is that enough?** A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. For anything above EUR 25 you need the itemised receipt or invoice. If the shop can print or email an itemised copy, ask for it at the till, because it is the safer document to upload. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-10. What does a receipt actually have to show?** It must show the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, and the total. If tax was charged, the tax amount must be shown too. A receipt that shows only a total is not enough, except for the card slip case up to EUR 25. Check for these details before you leave the shop or close the booking page. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-11. My receipt is in pounds. What amount do I claim?** Claims are in euros, and Finance does the conversion for you. Finance converts at the European Central Bank rate on the document date. The limits in the policy apply to the converted amount, so check your spend against the limit in euros. (Expense Policy Definitions) **FAQ-12. Finance sent my photo back because they could not read it. What now?** When a document is blurred, cut off or missing the total, the reviewer asks you for a new photo or file instead of rejecting the claim. Upload a clear copy that shows the whole receipt, including the total. Lay the receipt flat in good light, and make sure the edges are inside the picture. (Expense Policy 7.3) ## Meals and entertainment **FAQ-13. Can I grab a bite while I am away on a work trip, and how much can I spend?** Yes, during a business trip. A business trip is travel more than 50 km from your usual office, approved by your manager.

What is the most I can spend on a hotel room?** EUR 150 per night, or EUR 220 per night in a high-cost city: London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York or Oslo. For example, a night in a Paris hotel at EUR 205 is within the limit. A claim over the limit is rejected as a whole, and you submit it again with an amount within the limit. (Expense Policy 3.5, 7.1, Appendix A) **FAQ-33. Does the hotel breakfast count toward the limit? And the city tax?** When breakfast is included in the room rate, the limit covers the room and the breakfast together. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit, so they do not count toward it. The policy does not cover a hotel that bills breakfast as a separate item, so ask Finance in that case. (Expense Policy 3.5) **FAQ-34. Can I claim the minibar or a film I watched in my room?** No. Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. If these are on the same hotel bill as the room, the bill is a mixed receipt: the claim is rejected, and you submit it again without the personal items. (Expense Policy 3.6, 7.4) **FAQ-35. I am away for two weeks. Can I send my shirts to the hotel laundry?** Yes, but only on trips of 5 nights or longer. On a shorter trip, laundry is a personal expense. ## 1. Standard equipment issued at joining **IT1.1 Standard kit.** Every new employee receives a laptop, a phone and a headset from IT at no cost. The kit is ordered by IT and is not an expense, so the employee submits no claim for it. HR gives IT the start date at least 10 working days before the first day, so the kit is ready in time. **IT1.2 Laptop.** The standard laptop is a business laptop with a 14-inch screen, 16 GB of memory and a solid-state drive. IT installs the operating system, disk encryption, endpoint protection and the standard office tools before issue. Roles that need more memory or a larger screen, such as data engineering, receive a higher specification after a request through the IT portal. **IT1.3 Phone.** The standard phone is a current-generation smartphone with a company mobile plan. It is meant for calls, authentication codes and work messaging. It is enrolled in device management before issue, which lets IT lock or wipe it if it is lost. **IT1.4 Headset.** The standard headset is a wired over-ear USB headset with a microphone. It is chosen for call quality and costs the company far less than EUR 300. An employee who prefers a different headset may buy one under clause IT4.1. **IT1.5 Delivery.** Employees who work in an office collect the kit from IT on the first day. Remote employees receive it by courier at least 5 working days before the start date, and IT sends the first-login instructions separately by email to the employee's personal address. If the kit has not arrived 2 working days before the start date, the employee or the manager raises a request in the IT portal. **IT1.6 Replacement cycle.** Laptops are replaced every 3 years. Phones are replaced every 4 years. Headsets are replaced only when they stop working. IT starts the replacement automatically and tells the employee 30 days before it happens, so the employee does not need to request it. ## 2. Requesting additional equipment through the IT portal **IT2.1 The IT portal.** All requests for equipment that is not part of the standard kit are made in the IT portal, under "Request equipment". The request states what is needed, why, and the delivery address. Requests sent by email or chat are not tracked and are answered with a link to the portal. **IT2.2 Approval.** The employee's manager approves the business need in the portal. IT then checks stock and either allocates a device from stock or orders a new one. IT does not approve a request that the manager has not approved. **IT2.3 Delivery times.** IT delivers items it has in stock within 5 working days of the manager's approval. Items that IT must order are delivered within 15 working days.

Returning equipment when leaving **IT8.1 Return deadline.** The employee returns all Larkfield equipment within 14 days of the last working day. IT sends a prepaid courier box and a return label to remote employees. The employee should not wait for the box if they can return the equipment to an office. **IT8.2 What is returned.** The employee returns the laptop, the phone, the headset, the chargers and any item reimbursed under section 4, apart from the items that IT releases to the employee. IT checks the items against the list in the IT portal under "My equipment". **IT8.3 Data and accounts.** Before returning a device, the employee copies any personal files to a personal storage and does not delete work files. This section applies to purchases for the company, such as equipment for a team, software contracts and consulting services. **IT9.2 Team purchase orders up to EUR 3,000.** A team lead may approve a purchase order for the team up to EUR 3,000 within the team's budget. Definitions **0.1 Employee.** Anyone on the Larkfield payroll, including probation. **0.2 Claim.** One uploaded receipt or invoice together with the information the employee enters when submitting it (business purpose, attendees, pre-approval reference). **0.3 Business trip.** Travel more than 50 km from the employee's usual office, approved by the employee's manager. **0.4 High-cost city.** London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York, Oslo. **0.5 Pre-approval reference.** An identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN` issued by Finance before the purchase. **0.6 Reviewer.** A member of the Finance team who makes the final decision on a claim. **0.7 Currency.** All amounts are in euros (EUR). Where a receipt is in another currency, Finance converts it at the European Central Bank rate on the document date; limits apply to the converted amount. ## 1. General rules **1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. An expense is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. **1.2 Submission deadline.** A claim must be submitted within 60 days of the document date. Claims submitted later are rejected. The deadline exists because Finance closes each quarter's accounts and late claims cannot be booked to the right period. **1.3 Receipt requirements.** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice that shows the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, the total, and the tax amount where tax was charged. A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. Above EUR 25 the employee must provide the itemised receipt. **1.4 Duplicates.** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. If the employee genuinely made two identical purchases on the same day, they explain this in the business purpose. **1.5 Business purpose.** Every claim states its business purpose in a sentence: what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" alone is not a business purpose. ## 2. General rules **C1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that a contractor pays personally while delivering the work in the statement of work. An expense is reasonable when another contractor in the same engagement would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. Costs of running the contractor's own business are covered by the contractor's fees and are not reimbursed. **C1.2 Submission deadline.** An expense line must reach Finance on an invoice within 30 days of the document date. Lines that arrive later are rejected. Because contractors invoice monthly, an expense from early in a month can miss the deadline if it is held back for the next month's invoice. Flights should be booked at least 14 days before departure; a later booking is allowed when the trip itself was arranged at short notice, and the business purpose says so. **3.2 Rail travel.** Rail travel is booked in second class. First class is allowed for a single journey longer than 4 hours. **3.3 Taxis and ride-hailing.** A taxi or ride-hailing trip is reimbursed when public transport is not a reasonable option: when carrying equipment, when no public transport runs, or when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. The limit is EUR 60 per trip. Airport transfers in a high-cost city may exceed this limit when the receipt shows the airport as start or end of the trip. **3.4 Private car.** Use of a private car is reimbursed at EUR 0.30 per kilometre. ## Submitting a claim **FAQ-1. How do I get back money I paid out of my own pocket for work?** Submit a claim with the receipt and one sentence saying what the spend was for. Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job, and "employee" includes anyone on the payroll, even during probation. A cost is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5) **FAQ-2. Is it enough to write "work stuff" as the reason for the expense?** No. Write one sentence that says what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" on its own is not accepted as a business purpose. A good example is "Dinner with the client team during the Hamburg trip", because a reviewer can read it and know what the money bought. (Expense Policy 1.5) **FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?** You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?** Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-5. I uploaded the same receipt twice by mistake. Is that a problem?** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. Your first claim is not affected by this. You do not need to do anything about the first one. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-6. I really did buy two identical things at the same shop on the same day. Will the system think I cheated?** Two claims with the same vendor, total and document date look like duplicates, and the later one is rejected. I am not sure whether something is allowed. Who do I ask?** Ask Finance, which owns the policy.

Definitions **0.1 Employee.** Anyone on the Larkfield payroll, including probation. **0.2 Claim.** One uploaded receipt or invoice together with the information the employee enters when submitting it (business purpose, attendees, pre-approval reference). **0.3 Business trip.** Travel more than 50 km from the employee's usual office, approved by the employee's manager. **0.4 High-cost city.** London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York, Oslo. **0.5 Pre-approval reference.** An identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN` issued by Finance before the purchase. **0.6 Reviewer.** A member of the Finance team who makes the final decision on a claim. **0.7 Currency.** All amounts are in euros (EUR). General rules **1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. An expense is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. **1.2 Submission deadline.** A claim must be submitted within 60 days of the document date. Claims submitted later are rejected. The deadline exists because Finance closes each quarter's accounts and late claims cannot be booked to the right period. **1.3 Receipt requirements.** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice that shows the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, the total, and the tax amount where tax was charged. A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. Above EUR 25 the employee must provide the itemised receipt. **1.4 Duplicates.** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. If the employee genuinely made two identical purchases on the same day, they explain this in the business purpose. **1.5 Business purpose.** Every claim states its business purpose in a sentence: what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" alone is not a business purpose. ## 2. Meals **2.1 Meals during business trips.** During a business trip, Larkfield reimburses meals at their actual cost up to these limits per meal: breakfast EUR 15, lunch EUR 25, dinner EUR 45. Limits apply to the employee's own meal.

The 24 hours run from when the employee noticed, but employees should not wait. **IT7.2 What IT does.** On receiving the report IT locks the device and revokes its sessions, and it wipes the device if it is not recovered within 48 hours. A replacement does not restart the replacement cycle in clause IT1.6, so a laptop that is lost in its second year is replaced and is still due for renewal in year 3 of the original issue. Software and subscriptions **IT5.1 Software is bought through IT.** Software, cloud services, browser extensions and subscriptions used for work are requested in the IT portal and bought by IT through the company account (Expense Policy clause 4.2). The employee does not enter a payment card. **IT5.2 Why personal purchases are not reimbursed.** Software bought personally is not reimbursed, even when it is used for work (Expense Policy clause 4.2). IT cannot see, renew, move or cancel a personal licence, and it cannot check the vendor's data protection terms. A subscription that nobody at Larkfield owns also continues to charge after the employee leaves. **IT5.3 Free trials.** An employee may use a free trial for up to 30 days to test whether a tool is suitable, but only after telling IT in the portal. The trial uses the employee's work email address, never a personal card, and never customer data or production data. If the team wants to keep the tool, the manager requests a licence before the trial ends, because a trial that converts to a paid plan without IT is a personal purchase. **IT5.4 Open-source tools.** IT keeps a list of approved open-source tools that employees may install without a request. For a tool that is not on the list, the employee raises a request, and IT checks the licence terms, how active the maintainers are, and known security problems. Free software is still software for the purposes of this policy, and a tool is not exempt from review because it costs nothing. **IT5.5 Cancelling licences.** The manager reviews the licences of the team every quarter, and IT cancels the ones nobody uses. When an employee leaves, IT removes their licences on the last working day. A licence cannot be moved to a personal account. ## 6. Security requirements for any device used for work **IT6.1 Device protection.** Every device used for work must have full-disk encryption on, a screen lock that starts after at most 5 minutes of inactivity, and the endpoint protection agent that IT installed. Employees do not turn off or remove these controls. USB storage devices are blocked on Larkfield laptops unless IT gives an exception. **IT6.2 Accounts and passwords.** Work accounts use multi-factor authentication. Employees store passwords in the company password manager and never reuse a work password elsewhere. Passwords are not shared, written down or sent by email or chat, and a suspected leak is reported under clause IT7.1.

Returning equipment when leaving **IT8.1 Return deadline.** The employee returns all Larkfield equipment within 14 days of the last working day. IT sends a prepaid courier box and a return label to remote employees. The employee should not wait for the box if they can return the equipment to an office. **IT8.2 What is returned.** The employee returns the laptop, the phone, the headset, the chargers and any item reimbursed under section 4, apart from the items that IT releases to the employee. The employee also returns access cards, security keys and the original packaging if they still have it. IT checks the items against the list in the IT portal under "My equipment". **IT8.3 Data and accounts.** Before returning a device, the employee copies any personal files to a personal storage and does not delete work files. IT disables the work accounts on the last working day and wipes the returned devices afterwards. Personal data left on a returned device is not recovered after the wipe. **IT8.4 Equipment not returned.** If equipment has not arrived 30 days after the last working day, IT informs HR and Finance. Larkfield may recover the replacement value of the missing items as the employment contract and local law allow. Items that arrive later are accepted and the recovery is cancelled. ## 9. Purchasing from suppliers above EUR 5,000 **IT9.1 Company purchasing is not an employee expense.** When Larkfield buys goods or services from a supplier, a purchase order is raised and the supplier invoice is paid by Finance by bank transfer. Employees do not pay a supplier personally and then claim it under the Expense Policy. This section applies to purchases for the company, such as equipment for a team, software contracts and consulting services. **IT9.2 Team purchase orders up to EUR 3,000.** A team lead may approve a purchase order for the team up to EUR 3,000 within the team's budget. One written quote or a published price list is enough. A purchase order above EUR 3,000 needs the approval described in clause IT9.3. **IT9.3 Above EUR 3,000 and up to EUR 5,000.** A purchase order above EUR 3,000 and up to EUR 5,000 is approved by the head of the department. One written quote is still enough at this level. The department head checks that the purchase fits the budget and that the same need is not already covered by a contract. **IT9.4 Above EUR 5,000: three quotes.** A purchase above EUR 5,000 requires three written quotes from different suppliers. The requester compares them on price, delivery time, support and security, and records the reason for choosing one in the purchase order.

Home-office equipment **IT4.1 What employees may buy.** Employees may buy monitors, keyboards, headsets and chairs themselves and claim them under the Expense Policy. Employees who prefer IT-supplied items can still request them in the portal at no cost. For other office items, such as a desk or a webcam, the employee asks IT first, because Finance assesses them under clause 4.1 of the Expense Policy. **IT4.2 Limit of EUR 300 per item.** An item up to EUR 300 is reimbursed without a pre-approval reference (Expense Policy clause 4.1). The limit applies to each item and not to the whole order, so a EUR 250 monitor and a EUR 120 keyboard bought together are two items within the limit. The price counts after any discount and includes tax. **IT4.3 Items above EUR 300.** An item above EUR 300 needs a pre-approval reference issued before the purchase. The employee requests it as described in section 3 and attaches the product page or quote. The business purpose says what the item is used for, for example "second monitor for home office". IT lists them in the IT portal under "My equipment" so that they can be found and returned.

The requester compares them on price, delivery time, support and security, and records the reason for choosing one in the purchase order. When fewer than three suppliers can deliver the item, the requester records why, and the Head of Finance decides whether to accept fewer quotes. **IT9.5 Purchase orders.** Every purchase above EUR 3,000 is placed by a purchase order issued by Procurement, which is part of Finance. The order states the supplier, the items, the price, the delivery date and the budget owner. The supplier must quote the purchase order number on its invoice, and Finance does not pay an invoice that has no number. **IT9.6 Supplier checks.** Before the first order, Procurement checks the supplier's identity and bank details. A supplier that will handle personal data or customer data, or connect to Larkfield systems, also completes the security questionnaire that IT reviews. Only authorised signatories sign contracts, and an employee who is not authorised does not accept supplier terms on behalf of Larkfield. **IT9.7 No splitting.** A purchase is not divided into several smaller orders in order to stay under EUR 3,000 or EUR 5,000. Procurement adds together orders that cover the same need with the same supplier within the same quarter, and applies the approval level of the total. Repeated splitting is reported to the Head of Finance. ## Appendix. Examples - **Monitor within the limit.** An employee buys a monitor for EUR 280 for the home office and pays personally. Not reimbursed **6.1 Fines.** Parking tickets, speeding fines, and other penalties are never reimbursed, even when incurred on a business trip. **6.2 Personal items.** Clothing, toiletries, personal subscriptions, and gifts for colleagues are personal expenses. **6.3 Vouchers.** Gift cards, vouchers and prepaid cards are not reimbursed, because they cannot be matched to a business expense. **6.4 Loyalty schemes.** Points or miles earned on business expenses belong to the employee; their value is not reimbursed or deducted. ## 7. Decisions **7.1 Limits.** A claim that exceeds a limit in this policy is rejected as a whole. The employee may submit it again with the amount within the limit, explaining the difference in the business purpose. Finance does not part-approve claims, so that every booked amount matches a document. **7.2 Missing information.** When a claim is missing information the employee can provide (attendee list, business purpose, pre-approval reference, an itemised receipt), the reviewer asks for it instead of rejecting. The claim continues once the employee answers. **7.3 Unreadable documents.** When the document cannot be read (blurred, cut off, missing the total), the reviewer asks for a new photo or file. **7.4 Personal items on a business receipt.** When a receipt mixes business and personal items, the claim is rejected under clause 7.1, and the employee submits it again without the personal items. ## Appendix A. The manager does not decide whether an expense is within the limits of this policy; Finance does. **C7.5 Tax and currency.** Expense lines show the tax amount where the vendor charged tax, in line with the receipt. The contractor does not add a handling fee or mark-up to an expense. Larkfield pays expenses at their actual cost, converted under the currency rule above, and any mark-up is removed. **C7.6 Payment.** Approved expense lines are paid with the invoice, under the payment terms in the statement of work. Lines that Finance rejects are removed from the amount payable, and the rest of the invoice is paid on time. A rejected line does not delay payment of the fees. **C7.7 Corrections after submission.** A contractor who finds a mistake in an expense line after sending the invoice tells Finance and the engagement manager before the invoice is paid. Finance then asks for a corrected invoice, or removes the line and lets the contractor invoice it again next month if the 30-day deadline is still met. Corrections made after payment are handled as a credit note against the next invoice, so that the totals on both sides stay equal to the documents. ## 8. Decisions **C8.1 Limits.** An expense line that exceeds a limit in this policy is rejected as a whole. The contractor may invoice it again with the amount within the limit, explaining the difference in the business purpose, provided the document date is still within 30 days. Finance does not part-approve lines, so that every booked amount matches a document. **C8.2 Missing information.** When an expense line is missing information the contractor can provide (attendee list, business purpose, written approval, an itemised receipt), the reviewer asks for it instead of rejecting. The line continues once the contractor answers. The 30-day deadline in clause C1.2 still applies to the corrected line. **C8.3 Unreadable documents.** When the document cannot be read (blurred, cut off, missing the total), the reviewer asks for a new photo or file. **C8.4 Personal items on a business receipt.** When a receipt mixes business and personal items, or includes alcohol or other items that are never reimbursed, the line is rejected under clause C8.1, and the contractor invoices it again without those items. This keeps each booked amount equal to a document total. **C8.5 Disagreement.** A contractor who disagrees with a decision raises it with the engagement manager, who passes it to Finance with a short note. Finance reviews the decision against this policy and replies in writing with the clause it applied. The engagement manager cannot overrule a limit or an exclusion in this policy; only a statement of work that names the exception can do so. ## Appendix A. They are claimed in addition to mileage under clause C3.4, because the mileage rate does not cover them. A parking ticket issued for an offence is a fine and is never reimbursed under clause C6.1. ## 4. Equipment and software **C4.1 Equipment.** Equipment is never reimbursed to contractors. This covers monitors, keyboards, headsets, chairs, laptops and phones. Contractors supply their own equipment, and its cost is part of their fees. Where Larkfield needs a contractor to use Larkfield equipment, Larkfield supplies it directly through the engagement manager. **C4.2 Software.** Software and subscriptions are never reimbursed to contractors, even when they are used only for the engagement. Where the engagement needs a Larkfield system, IT gives the contractor access to it, so that licences stay on the company account and can be cancelled when the engagement ends. **C4.3 Accessories.** Accessories such as cables, adapters and phone cases are never reimbursed to contractors. The rule has no minimum amount, because small items are part of the contractor's own working costs. ## 5. Training and conferences **C5.1 Books and courses.** Books, online courses and certification exams are not reimbursed to contractors, unless the statement of work says so. A statement of work that allows training names the amount or the course. Without that wording, the cost is the contractor's own investment in their skills. **C5.2 Conferences.** Conference tickets are not reimbursed to contractors, unless the statement of work says so. When the statement of work does allow a conference, travel to the conference follows section 3 of this policy and the written approval of the engagement manager is attached to the expense line.

When the statement of work does allow a conference, travel to the conference follows section 3 of this policy and the written approval of the engagement manager is attached to the expense line. **C5.3 Training allowed by the statement of work.** When the statement of work allows training or a conference, the expense line quotes the clause of the statement of work that allows it. Finance checks the amount against the figure in the statement of work, and where the statement of work names no figure, against the written approval of the engagement manager. A line that quotes no clause is treated as training without permission and is rejected. ## 6. Not reimbursed **C6.1 Fines.** Parking tickets, speeding fines, and other penalties are never reimbursed, even when incurred on a business trip. **C6.2 Personal items.** Clothing, toiletries, personal subscriptions, and gifts for colleagues are personal expenses. **C6.3 Vouchers.** Gift cards, vouchers and prepaid cards are not reimbursed, because they cannot be matched to a business expense. **C6.4 Loyalty schemes.** Points or miles earned on business expenses belong to the contractor; their value is not reimbursed or deducted. **C6.5 Business overheads.** Costs of running the contractor's own business are not reimbursed. Examples are office rent, internet and phone contracts, insurance, accountancy, bank charges and professional memberships. These costs exist whether or not Larkfield engages the contractor, and the contractor's fees are set to cover them. ## 7. Invoicing expenses **C7.1 Monthly invoice.** Contractors invoice expenses once a month, together with their fees. Expenses are not submitted through the employee intake desk, which is for employee claims only and cannot process a contractor's expense line. A contractor who sends an expense to the intake desk is redirected to this process. **C7.2 Separate expense lines.** Expenses appear on the invoice as separate lines, apart from the fee lines. Each expense line shows the document date, the vendor, the amount in EUR, the original amount and currency where different, and the business purpose. Fees and expenses are separate so that Finance can check expenses against this policy without reviewing the fee calculation. **C7.3 Attached documents.** The receipt or invoice for each expense line is attached to the monthly invoice, in one file or several. The written approval of the engagement manager is attached where this policy requires it, for example for client entertainment. An expense line without its document is treated under clause C8.2. **C7.4 Approval by the engagement manager.** The engagement manager approves the monthly invoice, including its expense lines, before it goes to Finance. The manager confirms that the expenses relate to the engagement. The manager does not decide whether an expense is within the limits of this policy; Finance does.

40.text: ## Submitting a claim **FAQ-1. How do I get back money I paid out of my own pocket for work?** Submit a claim with the receipt and one sentence saying what the spend was for. Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job, and "employee" includes anyone on the payroll, even during probation. A cost is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5) **FAQ-2. Is it enough to write "work stuff" as the reason for the expense?** No. Write one sentence that says what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" on its own is not accepted as a business purpose. A good example is "Dinner with the client team during the Hamburg trip", because a reviewer can read it and know what the money bought. (Expense Policy 1.5) **FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?** You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?** Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-5. I uploaded the same receipt twice by mistake. Is that a problem?** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. Your first claim is not affected by this. You do not need to do anything about the first one. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-6. I really did buy two identical things at the same shop on the same day. Will the system think I cheated?** Two claims with the same vendor, total and document date look like duplicates, and the later one is rejected. If the two purchases were genuine, say so in the business purpose of the claim. That explanation is how the reviewer can tell the two claims apart. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-7. I am not sure whether something is allowed. Who do I ask?** Ask Finance, which owns the policy.

Who do I ask?** Ask Finance, which owns the policy. Ask before you buy, because a pre-approval reference is issued before the purchase, and the policy has no way to get one afterwards. If the policy is silent on your situation, Finance is the team that answers. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1) ## Receipts **FAQ-8. I lost the receipt. Can I still claim?** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice, and the policy has no rule that replaces a lost one. If you still have the payment card slip and the amount is EUR 25 or less, the slip is accepted. Above EUR 25 you must provide the itemised receipt. The policy does not say whether a bank or card statement can stand in, so ask Finance before you submit. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-9. The shop only gave me the slip from the card machine. Is that enough?** A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. For anything above EUR 25 you need the itemised receipt or invoice. If the shop can print or email an itemised copy, ask for it at the till, because it is the safer document to upload. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-10. What does a receipt actually have to show?** It must show the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, and the total. If tax was charged, the tax amount must be shown too. A receipt that shows only a total is not enough, except for the card slip case up to EUR 25. Check for these details before you leave the shop or close the booking page. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-11. My receipt is in pounds. What amount do I claim?** Claims are in euros, and Finance does the conversion for you. Finance converts at the European Central Bank rate on the document date. The limits in the policy apply to the converted amount, so check your spend against the limit in euros. (Expense Policy Definitions) **FAQ-12. Finance sent my photo back because they could not read it. What now?** When a document is blurred, cut off or missing the total, the reviewer asks you for a new photo or file instead of rejecting the claim. Upload a clear copy that shows the whole receipt, including the total. Lay the receipt flat in good light, and make sure the edges are inside the picture. (Expense Policy 7.3) ## Meals and entertainment **FAQ-13. Can I grab a bite while I am away on a work trip, and how much can I spend?** Yes, during a business trip. A business trip is travel more than 50 km from your usual office, approved by your manager.

General rules **1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. 4.text: Meals on days without travel are not reimbursed unless clause 2.2 or 2.4 applies. **2.2 Client entertainment.** A meal with clients or partners is reimbursed up to EUR 80 per attendee, counting every attendee including Larkfield employees. The claim must list the names and companies of all attendees and the business purpose of the meeting. Alcohol on a business trip meal without clients is not reimbursed. **2.4 Team meals.** A meal for a Larkfield team (no clients) is reimbursed only with a pre-approval reference. Team meals are usually celebrations or offsites that managers plan in advance; the reference confirms the budget was agreed. **2.5 Tips.** Tips are reimbursed up to 10% of the bill before the tip. Any tip above 10% is a personal expense. ## 3. Travel **3.1 Air travel.** Flights are booked in economy class. Premium economy is allowed for flights over 6 hours. Business and first class are not reimbursed. Flights should be booked at least 14 days before departure; a later booking is allowed when the trip itself was arranged at short notice, and the business purpose says so. **3.2 Rail travel.** Rail travel is booked in second class. First class is allowed for a single journey longer than 4 hours. **3.3 Taxis and ride-hailing.** A taxi or ride-hailing trip is reimbursed when public transport is not a reasonable option: when carrying equipment, when no public transport runs, or when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. The limit is EUR 60 per trip. Airport transfers in a high-cost city may exceed this limit when the receipt shows the airport as start or end of the trip. **3.4 Private car.** Use of a private car is reimbursed at EUR 0.30 per kilometre. The claim states the start and end address and the distance. Fuel receipts are not reimbursed separately when mileage is claimed. **3.5 Hotels.** Hotel rooms are reimbursed up to EUR 150 per night, or EUR 220 per night in a high-cost city. The limit covers the room and breakfast when breakfast is included in the rate. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit. **3.6 Hotel extras.** Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. Laundry is reimbursed only on trips of 5 nights or longer. ## 4.

Can I rent a car for a client visit?** The policy does not mention rental cars. It covers the use of your own private car at EUR 0.30 per kilometre, and the general rule is that a cost must be reasonable for your role and purpose. Ask Finance before you book a rental so you know it will be accepted.
