(Expense Policy 6.3) **FAQ-46. I forgot my toothbrush and a clean shirt for the trip. Can I claim what I bought?** No. Clothing and toiletries are personal expenses, even when you buy them on a business trip. (Expense Policy 6.2) **FAQ-47. I earned airline miles on a business flight. Do I have to give them back?** No. Points and miles earned on business expenses belong to you. Their value is neither reimbursed nor deducted. Your claim is for the money you spent, and the points you earned do not reduce it. (Expense Policy 6.4) ## Decisions and appeals **FAQ-48. My claim says "needs info". What does that mean?** The reviewer is missing something you can provide, such as the attendee list, the business purpose, a pre-approval reference or an itemised receipt. If the document could not be read, the reviewer asks for a new photo or file. It is not a rejection. The claim continues once you answer. (Expense Policy 7.2, 7.3) **FAQ-49. My claim was rejected because it was over a limit. What now?** Submit it again with the amount within the limit, and explain the difference in the business purpose. For example, a EUR 52 dinner on a trip is over the EUR 45 dinner limit and is rejected, while a claim for EUR 45 with a note is accepted. The policy describes no separate appeal. If you think the decision was wrong, ask Finance. The policy does not say that a new submission restarts the 60-day deadline, so do not wait. (Expense Policy 7.1, 1.2, Appendix A) **FAQ-50. Can Finance just pay the part that is within the limit?** No. Finance does not part-approve claims, so that every booked amount matches a document. A claim over a limit is rejected as a whole, and you submit it again with the amount within the limit. (Expense Policy 7.1) **FAQ-51. My receipt has a few personal items mixed in with the work ones. What happens?** The claim is rejected, and you submit it again without the personal items. Finance does not part-approve claims. (Expense Policy 7.4, 7.1) **FAQ-52. How long does Finance take to review a claim?** Finance aims for 5 working days. The policy itself sets no review time. If the reviewer asks you for information, the claim continues once you answer, so a quick answer keeps it moving. (Expense Policy 7.2) ## Using the intake desk **FAQ-53. What do I have to fill in when I upload a receipt?** A claim is one uploaded receipt or invoice plus the information you enter. Always enter the business purpose.

8.text: ## Submitting a claim **FAQ-1. How do I get back money I paid out of my own pocket for work?** Submit a claim with the receipt and one sentence saying what the spend was for. Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job, and "employee" includes anyone on the payroll, even during probation. A cost is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5) **FAQ-2. Is it enough to write "work stuff" as the reason for the expense?** No. Write one sentence that says what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" on its own is not accepted as a business purpose. A good example is "Dinner with the client team during the Hamburg trip", because a reviewer can read it and know what the money bought. (Expense Policy 1.5) **FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?** You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?** Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-5. I uploaded the same receipt twice by mistake. Is that a problem?** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. Your first claim is not affected by this. You do not need to do anything about the first one. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-6. I really did buy two identical things at the same shop on the same day. Will the system think I cheated?** Two claims with the same vendor, total and document date look like duplicates, and the later one is rejected. If the two purchases were genuine, say so in the business purpose of the claim. That explanation is how the reviewer can tell the two claims apart. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-7. I am not sure whether something is allowed. Who do I ask?** Ask Finance, which owns the policy.

Who do I ask?** Ask Finance, which owns the policy. Ask before you buy, because a pre-approval reference is issued before the purchase, and the policy has no way to get one afterwards. If the policy is silent on your situation, Finance is the team that answers. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1) ## Receipts **FAQ-8. I lost the receipt. Can I still claim?** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice, and the policy has no rule that replaces a lost one. If you still have the payment card slip and the amount is EUR 25 or less, the slip is accepted. Above EUR 25 you must provide the itemised receipt. The policy does not say whether a bank or card statement can stand in, so ask Finance before you submit. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-9. The shop only gave me the slip from the card machine. Is that enough?** A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. For anything above EUR 25 you need the itemised receipt or invoice. If the shop can print or email an itemised copy, ask for it at the till, because it is the safer document to upload. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-10. What does a receipt actually have to show?** It must show the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, and the total. If tax was charged, the tax amount must be shown too. A receipt that shows only a total is not enough, except for the card slip case up to EUR 25. Check for these details before you leave the shop or close the booking page. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-11. My receipt is in pounds. What amount do I claim?** Claims are in euros, and Finance does the conversion for you. Finance converts at the European Central Bank rate on the document date. The limits in the policy apply to the converted amount, so check your spend against the limit in euros. (Expense Policy Definitions) **FAQ-12. Finance sent my photo back because they could not read it. What now?** When a document is blurred, cut off or missing the total, the reviewer asks you for a new photo or file instead of rejecting the claim. Upload a clear copy that shows the whole receipt, including the total. Lay the receipt flat in good light, and make sure the edges are inside the picture. (Expense Policy 7.3) ## Meals and entertainment **FAQ-13. Can I grab a bite while I am away on a work trip, and how much can I spend?** Yes, during a business trip. A business trip is travel more than 50 km from your usual office, approved by your manager.

What is the most I can spend on a hotel room?** EUR 150 per night, or EUR 220 per night in a high-cost city: London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York or Oslo. For example, a night in a Paris hotel at EUR 205 is within the limit. A claim over the limit is rejected as a whole, and you submit it again with an amount within the limit. (Expense Policy 3.5, 7.1, Appendix A) **FAQ-33. Does the hotel breakfast count toward the limit? And the city tax?** When breakfast is included in the room rate, the limit covers the room and the breakfast together. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit, so they do not count toward it. The policy does not cover a hotel that bills breakfast as a separate item, so ask Finance in that case. (Expense Policy 3.5) **FAQ-34. Can I claim the minibar or a film I watched in my room?** No. Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. If these are on the same hotel bill as the room, the bill is a mixed receipt: the claim is rejected, and you submit it again without the personal items. (Expense Policy 3.6, 7.4) **FAQ-35. I am away for two weeks. Can I send my shirts to the hotel laundry?** Yes, but only on trips of 5 nights or longer. On a shorter trip, laundry is a personal expense. Minibar, in-room entertainment and spa stay personal on any trip, however long. (Expense Policy 3.6) ## Equipment and software **FAQ-36. Can I buy a monitor or a better chair myself and claim it?** Office equipment such as monitors, keyboards, headsets and chairs is reimbursed up to EUR 300 per item without pre-approval. An item above EUR 300 needs a pre-approval reference from Finance before you buy it. (Expense Policy 4.1) **FAQ-37. Can I buy a new laptop or phone myself?** Laptops and phones are supplied by IT. If you buy one yourself, it needs a pre-approval reference at any price. Get the reference from Finance before the purchase. IT supplies the device, so ask IT first. (Expense Policy 4.1) **FAQ-38. I paid for a software subscription that I use for work. Can I claim it?** No.

## 1. Standard equipment issued at joining **IT1.1 Standard kit.** Every new employee receives a laptop, a phone and a headset from IT at no cost. The kit is ordered by IT and is not an expense, so the employee submits no claim for it. HR gives IT the start date at least 10 working days before the first day, so the kit is ready in time. **IT1.2 Laptop.** The standard laptop is a business laptop with a 14-inch screen, 16 GB of memory and a solid-state drive. IT installs the operating system, disk encryption, endpoint protection and the standard office tools before issue. Roles that need more memory or a larger screen, such as data engineering, receive a higher specification after a request through the IT portal. **IT1.3 Phone.** The standard phone is a current-generation smartphone with a company mobile plan. It is meant for calls, authentication codes and work messaging. It is enrolled in device management before issue, which lets IT lock or wipe it if it is lost. **IT1.4 Headset.** The standard headset is a wired over-ear USB headset with a microphone. It is chosen for call quality and costs the company far less than EUR 300. An employee who prefers a different headset may buy one under clause IT4.1. **IT1.5 Delivery.** Employees who work in an office collect the kit from IT on the first day. Remote employees receive it by courier at least 5 working days before the start date, and IT sends the first-login instructions separately by email to the employee's personal address. If the kit has not arrived 2 working days before the start date, the employee or the manager raises a request in the IT portal. **IT1.6 Replacement cycle.** Laptops are replaced every 3 years. Phones are replaced every 4 years. Headsets are replaced only when they stop working. IT starts the replacement automatically and tells the employee 30 days before it happens, so the employee does not need to request it. ## 2. Requesting additional equipment through the IT portal **IT2.1 The IT portal.** All requests for equipment that is not part of the standard kit are made in the IT portal, under "Request equipment". The request states what is needed, why, and the delivery address. Requests sent by email or chat are not tracked and are answered with a link to the portal. **IT2.2 Approval.** The employee's manager approves the business need in the portal. IT then checks stock and either allocates a device from stock or orders a new one. IT does not approve a request that the manager has not approved. **IT2.3 Delivery times.** IT delivers items it has in stock within 5 working days of the manager's approval. Items that IT must order are delivered within 15 working days.

Larkfield does not deduct the cost of a device from salary. ## 8. Returning equipment when leaving **IT8.1 Return deadline.** The employee returns all Larkfield equipment within 14 days of the last working day. IT sends a prepaid courier box and a return label to remote employees. The employee should not wait for the box if they can return the equipment to an office. **IT8.2 What is returned.** The employee returns the laptop, the phone, the headset, the chargers and any item reimbursed under section 4, apart from the items that IT releases to the employee. The employee also returns access cards, security keys and the original packaging if they still have it. IT checks the items against the list in the IT portal under "My equipment". **IT8.3 Data and accounts.** Before returning a device, the employee copies any personal files to a personal storage and does not delete work files. IT disables the work accounts on the last working day and wipes the returned devices afterwards. Personal data left on a returned device is not recovered after the wipe. **IT8.4 Equipment not returned.** If equipment has not arrived 30 days after the last working day, IT informs HR and Finance. Larkfield may recover the replacement value of the missing items as the employment contract and local law allow. Items that arrive later are accepted and the recovery is cancelled. ## 9. Purchasing from suppliers above EUR 5,000 **IT9.1 Company purchasing is not an employee expense.** When Larkfield buys goods or services from a supplier, a purchase order is raised and the supplier invoice is paid by Finance by bank transfer. Employees do not pay a supplier personally and then claim it under the Expense Policy. This section applies to purchases for the company, such as equipment for a team, software contracts and consulting services. **IT9.2 Team purchase orders up to EUR 3,000.** A team lead may approve a purchase order for the team up to EUR 3,000 within the team's budget. One written quote or a published price list is enough. A purchase order above EUR 3,000 needs the approval described in clause IT9.3. **IT9.3 Above EUR 3,000 and up to EUR 5,000.** A purchase order above EUR 3,000 and up to EUR 5,000 is approved by the head of the department. One written quote is still enough at this level. The department head checks that the purchase fits the budget and that the same need is not already covered by a contract. **IT9.4 Above EUR 5,000: three quotes.** A purchase above EUR 5,000 requires three written quotes from different suppliers. The requester compares them on price, delivery time, support and security, and records the reason for choosing one in the purchase order.

Software and subscriptions **IT5.1 Software is bought through IT.** Software, cloud services, browser extensions and subscriptions used for work are requested in the IT portal and bought by IT through the company account (Expense Policy clause 4.2). IT assigns a licence to the employee's work account. The employee does not enter a payment card. **IT5.2 Why personal purchases are not reimbursed.** Software bought personally is not reimbursed, even when it is used for work (Expense Policy clause 4.2). IT cannot see, renew, move or cancel a personal licence, and it cannot check the vendor's data protection terms. A subscription that nobody at Larkfield owns also continues to charge after the employee leaves. **IT5.3 Free trials.** An employee may use a free trial for up to 30 days to test whether a tool is suitable, but only after telling IT in the portal. The trial uses the employee's work email address, never a personal card, and never customer data or production data. If the team wants to keep the tool, the manager requests a licence before the trial ends, because a trial that converts to a paid plan without IT is a personal purchase. **IT5.4 Open-source tools.** IT keeps a list of approved open-source tools that employees may install without a request. For a tool that is not on the list, the employee raises a request, and IT checks the licence terms, how active the maintainers are, and known security problems. Free software is still software for the purposes of this policy, and a tool is not exempt from review because it costs nothing. **IT5.5 Cancelling licences.** The manager reviews the licences of the team every quarter, and IT cancels the ones nobody uses. When an employee leaves, IT removes their licences on the last working day. A licence cannot be moved to a personal account. ## 6. Security requirements for any device used for work **IT6.1 Device protection.** Every device used for work must have full-disk encryption on, a screen lock that starts after at most 5 minutes of inactivity, and the endpoint protection agent that IT installed. Employees do not turn off or remove these controls. USB storage devices are blocked on Larkfield laptops unless IT gives an exception. **IT6.2 Accounts and passwords.** Work accounts use multi-factor authentication. Employees store passwords in the company password manager and never reuse a work password elsewhere. Passwords are not shared, written down or sent by email or chat, and a suspected leak is reported under clause IT7.1.

Definitions **0.1 Employee.** Anyone on the Larkfield payroll, including probation. **0.2 Claim.** One uploaded receipt or invoice together with the information the employee enters when submitting it (business purpose, attendees, pre-approval reference). **0.3 Business trip.** Travel more than 50 km from the employee's usual office, approved by the employee's manager. **0.4 High-cost city.** London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York, Oslo. **0.5 Pre-approval reference.** An identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN` issued by Finance before the purchase. **0.6 Reviewer.** A member of the Finance team who makes the final decision on a claim. **0.7 Currency.** All amounts are in euros (EUR). Where a receipt is in another currency, Finance converts it at the European Central Bank rate on the document date; limits apply to the converted amount. ## 1. General rules **1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. An expense is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. **1.2 Submission deadline.** A claim must be submitted within 60 days of the document date. Claims submitted later are rejected. The deadline exists because Finance closes each quarter's accounts and late claims cannot be booked to the right period. **1.3 Receipt requirements.** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice that shows the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, the total, and the tax amount where tax was charged. A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. Above EUR 25 the employee must provide the itemised receipt. **1.4 Duplicates.** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. If the employee genuinely made two identical purchases on the same day, they explain this in the business purpose. **1.5 Business purpose.** Every claim states its business purpose in a sentence: what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" alone is not a business purpose. ## 2. Meals **2.1 Meals during business trips.** During a business trip, Larkfield reimburses meals at their actual cost up to these limits per meal: breakfast EUR 15, lunch EUR 25, dinner EUR 45. Limits apply to the employee's own meal.

Meals on days without travel are not reimbursed unless clause 2.2 or 2.4 applies. **2.2 Client entertainment.** A meal with clients or partners is reimbursed up to EUR 80 per attendee, counting every attendee including Larkfield employees. The claim must list the names and companies of all attendees and the business purpose of the meeting. A client entertainment claim without the attendee list cannot be assessed against the limit. **2.3 Alcohol.** Alcohol is reimbursed only as part of client entertainment under clause 2.2, and within its per-attendee limit. Alcohol on a business trip meal without clients is not reimbursed. **2.4 Team meals.** A meal for a Larkfield team (no clients) is reimbursed only with a pre-approval reference. Team meals are usually celebrations or offsites that managers plan in advance; the reference confirms the budget was agreed. **2.5 Tips.** Tips are reimbursed up to 10% of the bill before the tip. Any tip above 10% is a personal expense. ## 3. Travel **3.1 Air travel.** Flights are booked in economy class. Premium economy is allowed for flights over 6 hours. Business and first class are not reimbursed. Flights should be booked at least 14 days before departure; a later booking is allowed when the trip itself was arranged at short notice, and the business purpose says so. **3.2 Rail travel.** Rail travel is booked in second class. First class is allowed for a single journey longer than 4 hours. **3.3 Taxis and ride-hailing.** A taxi or ride-hailing trip is reimbursed when public transport is not a reasonable option: when carrying equipment, when no public transport runs, or when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. The limit is EUR 60 per trip. Airport transfers in a high-cost city may exceed this limit when the receipt shows the airport as start or end of the trip. **3.4 Private car.** Use of a private car is reimbursed at EUR 0.30 per kilometre. The claim states the start and end address and the distance. Fuel receipts are not reimbursed separately when mileage is claimed. **3.5 Hotels.** Hotel rooms are reimbursed up to EUR 150 per night, or EUR 220 per night in a high-cost city. The limit covers the room and breakfast when breakfast is included in the rate. City taxes are reimbursed in addition to the limit. **3.6 Hotel extras.** Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses. Laundry is reimbursed only on trips of 5 nights or longer. ## 4.

If the policy is silent on your situation, Finance is the team that answers. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1) ## Receipts **FAQ-8. I lost the receipt. Can I still claim?** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice, and the policy has no rule that replaces a lost one. If you still have the payment card slip and the amount is EUR 25 or less, the slip is accepted. Above EUR 25 you must provide the itemised receipt. The policy does not say whether a bank or card statement can stand in, so ask Finance before you submit. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-9. The shop only gave me the slip from the card machine. Is that enough?** A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. For anything above EUR 25 you need the itemised receipt or invoice. If the shop can print or email an itemised copy, ask for it at the till, because it is the safer document to upload. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-10. What does a receipt actually have to show?** It must show the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, and the total. If tax was charged, the tax amount must be shown too. A receipt that shows only a total is not enough, except for the card slip case up to EUR 25. Check for these details before you leave the shop or close the booking page. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-11. My receipt is in pounds. What amount do I claim?** Claims are in euros, and Finance does the conversion for you. Finance converts at the European Central Bank rate on the document date. The limits in the policy apply to the converted amount, so check your spend against the limit in euros. (Expense Policy Definitions) **FAQ-12. Finance sent my photo back because they could not read it. IT assigns a licence to the employee's work account. The employee does not enter a payment card. **IT5.2 Why personal purchases are not reimbursed.** Software bought personally is not reimbursed, even when it is used for work (Expense Policy clause 4.2). IT cannot see, renew, move or cancel a personal licence, and it cannot check the vendor's data protection terms. A subscription that nobody at Larkfield owns also continues to charge after the employee leaves. **IT5.3 Free trials.** An employee may use a free trial for up to 30 days to test whether a tool is suitable, but only after telling IT in the portal. The trial uses the employee's work email address, never a personal card, and never customer data or production data. If the team wants to keep the tool, the manager requests a licence before the trial ends, because a trial that converts to a paid plan without IT is a personal purchase. **IT5.4 Open-source tools.** IT keeps a list of approved open-source tools that employees may install without a request. For a tool that is not on the list, the employee raises a request, and IT checks the licence terms, how active the maintainers are, and known security problems. Free software is still software for the purposes of this policy, and a tool is not exempt from review because it costs nothing. **IT5.5 Cancelling licences.** The manager reviews the licences of the team every quarter, and IT cancels the ones nobody uses. When an employee leaves, IT removes their licences on the last working day. A licence cannot be moved to a personal account. ## 6. Security requirements for any device used for work **IT6.1 Device protection.** Every device used for work must have full-disk encryption on, a screen lock that starts after at most 5 minutes of inactivity, and the endpoint protection agent that IT installed. Employees do not turn off or remove these controls. USB storage devices are blocked on Larkfield laptops unless IT gives an exception. **IT6.2 Accounts and passwords.** Work accounts use multi-factor authentication. Employees store passwords in the company password manager and never reuse a work password elsewhere. Passwords are not shared, written down or sent by email or chat, and a suspected leak is reported under clause IT7.1.

Definitions **0.1 Employee.** Anyone on the Larkfield payroll, including probation. **0.2 Claim.** One uploaded receipt or invoice together with the information the employee enters when submitting it (business purpose, attendees, pre-approval reference). **0.3 Business trip.** Travel more than 50 km from the employee's usual office, approved by the employee's manager. **0.4 High-cost city.** London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York, Oslo. **0.5 Pre-approval reference.** An identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN` issued by Finance before the purchase. **0.6 Reviewer.** A member of the Finance team who makes the final decision on a claim. **0.7 Currency.** All amounts are in euros (EUR). Where a receipt is in another currency, Finance converts it at the European Central Bank rate on the document date; limits apply to the converted amount. ## 1. General rules **1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. An expense is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. **1.2 Submission deadline.** A claim must be submitted within 60 days of the document date. Claims submitted later are rejected. The deadline exists because Finance closes each quarter's accounts and late claims cannot be booked to the right period. **1.3 Receipt requirements.** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice that shows the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, the total, and the tax amount where tax was charged. A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. Above EUR 25 the employee must provide the itemised receipt. **1.4 Duplicates.** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. If the employee genuinely made two identical purchases on the same day, they explain this in the business purpose. **1.5 Business purpose.** Every claim states its business purpose in a sentence: what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" alone is not a business purpose. ## 2. Meals **2.1 Meals during business trips.** During a business trip, Larkfield reimburses meals at their actual cost up to these limits per meal: breakfast EUR 15, lunch EUR 25, dinner EUR 45. Limits apply to the employee's own meal.

For a tool that is not on the list, the employee raises a request, and IT checks the licence terms, how active the maintainers are, and known security problems. Free software is still software for the purposes of this policy, and a tool is not exempt from review because it costs nothing. **IT5.5 Cancelling licences.** The manager reviews the licences of the team every quarter, and IT cancels the ones nobody uses. When an employee leaves, IT removes their licences on the last working day. A licence cannot be moved to a personal account. ## 6. Employees do not turn off or remove these controls. USB storage devices are blocked on Larkfield laptops unless IT gives an exception. **IT6.2 Accounts and passwords.** Work accounts use multi-factor authentication. Employees store passwords in the company password manager and never reuse a work password elsewhere. Passwords are not shared, written down or sent by email or chat, and a suspected leak is reported under clause IT7.1.

Returning equipment when leaving **IT8.1 Return deadline.** The employee returns all Larkfield equipment within 14 days of the last working day. IT sends a prepaid courier box and a return label to remote employees. The employee should not wait for the box if they can return the equipment to an office. **IT8.2 What is returned.** The employee returns the laptop, the phone, the headset, the chargers and any item reimbursed under section 4, apart from the items that IT releases to the employee. The employee also returns access cards, security keys and the original packaging if they still have it. IT checks the items against the list in the IT portal under "My equipment". **IT8.3 Data and accounts.** Before returning a device, the employee copies any personal files to a personal storage and does not delete work files. IT disables the work accounts on the last working day and wipes the returned devices afterwards. Personal data left on a returned device is not recovered after the wipe. **IT8.4 Equipment not returned.** If equipment has not arrived 30 days after the last working day, IT informs HR and Finance. Larkfield may recover the replacement value of the missing items as the employment contract and local law allow. Items that arrive later are accepted and the recovery is cancelled. ## 9. Purchasing from suppliers above EUR 5,000 **IT9.1 Company purchasing is not an employee expense.** When Larkfield buys goods or services from a supplier, a purchase order is raised and the supplier invoice is paid by Finance by bank transfer. Employees do not pay a supplier personally and then claim it under the Expense Policy. This section applies to purchases for the company, such as equipment for a team, software contracts and consulting services. **IT9.2 Team purchase orders up to EUR 3,000.** A team lead may approve a purchase order for the team up to EUR 3,000 within the team's budget. One written quote or a published price list is enough. A purchase order above EUR 3,000 needs the approval described in clause IT9.3. **IT9.3 Above EUR 3,000 and up to EUR 5,000.** A purchase order above EUR 3,000 and up to EUR 5,000 is approved by the head of the department. One written quote is still enough at this level. The department head checks that the purchase fits the budget and that the same need is not already covered by a contract. **IT9.4 Above EUR 5,000: three quotes.** A purchase above EUR 5,000 requires three written quotes from different suppliers. The requester compares them on price, delivery time, support and security, and records the reason for choosing one in the purchase order.

Home-office equipment **IT4.1 What employees may buy.** Employees may buy monitors, keyboards, headsets and chairs themselves and claim them under the Expense Policy. Employees who prefer IT-supplied items can still request them in the portal at no cost. For other office items, such as a desk or a webcam, the employee asks IT first, because Finance assesses them under clause 4.1 of the Expense Policy. **IT4.2 Limit of EUR 300 per item.** An item up to EUR 300 is reimbursed without a pre-approval reference (Expense Policy clause 4.1). The limit applies to each item and not to the whole order, so a EUR 250 monitor and a EUR 120 keyboard bought together are two items within the limit. The price counts after any discount and includes tax. **IT4.3 Items above EUR 300.** An item above EUR 300 needs a pre-approval reference issued before the purchase. The employee requests it as described in section 3 and attaches the product page or quote. If the employee buys such an item without a reference, Finance cannot reimburse it. **IT4.4 Receipts.** The claim needs the itemised receipt or invoice required by Expense Policy clause 1.3. The business purpose says what the item is used for, for example "second monitor for home office". The employee submits the claim within 60 days of the document date. **IT4.5 Ownership.** Items reimbursed under this section become the property of Larkfield. The requester compares them on price, delivery time, support and security, and records the reason for choosing one in the purchase order. The order states the supplier, the items, the price, the delivery date and the budget owner. The supplier must quote the purchase order number on its invoice, and Finance does not pay an invoice that has no number. **IT9.6 Supplier checks.** Before the first order, Procurement checks the supplier's identity and bank details. A supplier that will handle personal data or customer data, or connect to Larkfield systems, also completes the security questionnaire that IT reviews. Only authorised signatories sign contracts, and an employee who is not authorised does not accept supplier terms on behalf of Larkfield. **IT9.7 No splitting.** A purchase is not divided into several smaller orders in order to stay under EUR 3,000 or EUR 5,000. Procurement adds together orders that cover the same need with the same supplier within the same quarter, and applies the approval level of the total. Repeated splitting is reported to the Head of Finance. ## Appendix. Examples - **Monitor within the limit.** An employee buys a monitor for EUR 280 for the home office and pays personally. If you still have the payment card slip and the amount is EUR 25 or less, the slip is accepted. Above EUR 25 you must provide the itemised receipt. The policy does not say whether a bank or card statement can stand in, so ask Finance before you submit. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-9. The shop only gave me the slip from the card machine. Is that enough?** A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. For anything above EUR 25 you need the itemised receipt or invoice. If the shop can print or email an itemised copy, ask for it at the till, because it is the safer document to upload. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-10. What does a receipt actually have to show?** It must show the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, and the total. If tax was charged, the tax amount must be shown too. A receipt that shows only a total is not enough, except for the card slip case up to EUR 25. Check for these details before you leave the shop or close the booking page. (Expense Policy 1.3) **FAQ-11. My receipt is in pounds. What amount do I claim?** Claims are in euros, and Finance does the conversion for you. (Expense Policy Definitions) **FAQ-12. Finance sent my photo back because they could not read it. Decisions **7.1 Limits.** A claim that exceeds a limit in this policy is rejected as a whole. The claim continues once the employee answers. **7.3 Unreadable documents.** When the document cannot be read (blurred, cut off, missing the total), the reviewer asks for a new photo or file. **7.4 Personal items on a business receipt.** When a receipt mixes business and personal items, the claim is rejected under clause 7.1, and the employee submits it again without the personal items. ## Appendix A. ## Submitting a claim **FAQ-1. How do I get back money I paid out of my own pocket for work?** Submit a claim with the receipt and one sentence saying what the spend was for. Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job, and "employee" includes anyone on the payroll, even during probation. A cost is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5) **FAQ-2. Is it enough to write "work stuff" as the reason for the expense?** No. Write one sentence that says what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" on its own is not accepted as a business purpose. A good example is "Dinner with the client team during the Hamburg trip", because a reviewer can read it and know what the money bought. (Expense Policy 1.5) **FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?** You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?** Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2) **FAQ-5. I uploaded the same receipt twice by mistake. Is that a problem?** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. Your first claim is not affected by this. You do not need to do anything about the first one. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-6. I really did buy two identical things at the same shop on the same day. Will the system think I cheated?** Two claims with the same vendor, total and document date look like duplicates, and the later one is rejected. If the two purchases were genuine, say so in the business purpose of the claim. That explanation is how the reviewer can tell the two claims apart. (Expense Policy 1.4) **FAQ-7. I am not sure whether something is allowed. Who do I ask?** Ask Finance, which owns the policy.

## 0. Definitions **0.1 Employee.** Anyone on the Larkfield payroll, including probation. **0.2 Claim.** One uploaded receipt or invoice together with the information the employee enters when submitting it (business purpose, attendees, pre-approval reference). **0.3 Business trip.** Travel more than 50 km from the employee's usual office, approved by the employee's manager. **0.4 High-cost city.** London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York, Oslo. **0.5 Pre-approval reference.** An identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN` issued by Finance before the purchase. **0.6 Reviewer.** A member of the Finance team who makes the final decision on a claim. **0.7 Currency.** All amounts are in euros (EUR). Where a receipt is in another currency, Finance converts it at the European Central Bank rate on the document date; limits apply to the converted amount. ## 1. General rules **1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. An expense is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. **1.2 Submission deadline.** A claim must be submitted within 60 days of the document date. Claims submitted later are rejected. The deadline exists because Finance closes each quarter's accounts and late claims cannot be booked to the right period. **1.3 Receipt requirements.** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice that shows the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, the total, and the tax amount where tax was charged. A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. Above EUR 25 the employee must provide the itemised receipt. **1.4 Duplicates.** The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. Equipment and software **4.1 Equipment.** Office equipment (monitors, keyboards, headsets, chairs) up to EUR 300 per item is reimbursed without pre-approval. An item above EUR 300 needs a pre-approval reference. Laptops and phones are supplied by IT and need a pre-approval reference at any price. **4.2 Software.** Software and subscriptions are bought by IT through the company account so licences can be managed and cancelled. Not reimbursed **6.1 Fines.** Parking tickets, speeding fines, and other penalties are never reimbursed, even when incurred on a business trip. **6.2 Personal items.** Clothing, toiletries, personal subscriptions, and gifts for colleagues are personal expenses. **6.3 Vouchers.** Gift cards, vouchers and prepaid cards are not reimbursed, because they cannot be matched to a business expense. **6.4 Loyalty schemes.** Points or miles earned on business expenses belong to the employee; their value is not reimbursed or deducted. ## 7. Decisions **7.1 Limits.** A claim that exceeds a limit in this policy is rejected as a whole. The employee may submit it again with the amount within the limit, explaining the difference in the business purpose. Finance does not part-approve claims, so that every booked amount matches a document. **7.2 Missing information.** When a claim is missing information the employee can provide (attendee list, business purpose, pre-approval reference, an itemised receipt), the reviewer asks for it instead of rejecting. The claim continues once the employee answers. **7.3 Unreadable documents.** When the document cannot be read (blurred, cut off, missing the total), the reviewer asks for a new photo or file. **7.4 Personal items on a business receipt.** When a receipt mixes business and personal items, the claim is rejected under clause 7.1, and the employee submits it again without the personal items. ## Appendix A. ## Submitting a claim
**FAQ-1. How do I get back money I paid out of my own pocket for work?**
Submit a claim with the receipt and one sentence saying what the spend was for. Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job, and "employee" includes anyone on the payroll, even during probation. A cost is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5)
**FAQ-2. Is it enough to write "work stuff" as the reason for the expense?**
No. Write one sentence that says what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" on its own is not accepted as a business purpose. A good example is "Dinner with the client team during the Hamburg trip", because a reviewer can read it and know what the money bought. (Expense Policy 1.5)
**FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?**
You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2)
**FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?**
Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2)
**FAQ-5. I uploaded the same receipt twice by mistake.

For anything above EUR 25 you need the itemised receipt or invoice. If the shop can print or email an itemised copy, ask for it at the till, because it is the safer document to upload. (Expense Policy 1.3)
**FAQ-10. What does a receipt actually have to show?**
It must show the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, and the total. If tax was charged, the tax amount must be shown too. A receipt that shows only a total is not enough, except for the card slip case up to EUR 25. Check for these details before you leave the shop or close the booking page. (Expense Policy 1.3)
**FAQ-11. My receipt is in pounds. What amount do I claim?**
Claims are in euros, and Finance does the conversion for you. Finance converts at the European Central Bank rate on the document date. The limits in the policy apply to the converted amount, so check your spend against the limit in euros. (Expense Policy Definitions)
**FAQ-12. Finance sent my photo back because they could not read it. What now?**
When a document is blurred, cut off or missing the total, the reviewer asks you for a new photo or file instead of rejecting the claim. Upload a clear copy that shows the whole receipt, including the total. Lay the receipt flat in good light, and make sure the edges are inside the picture. (Expense Policy 7.3)
## Meals and entertainment
**FAQ-13. Can I grab a bite while I am away on a work trip, and how much can I spend?**
Yes, during a business trip. A business trip is travel more than 50 km from your usual office, approved by your manager. Meals are reimbursed at actual cost up to EUR 15 for breakfast, EUR 25 for lunch and EUR 45 for dinner. These limits apply to your own meal only.
A card slip of EUR 18 without an itemised receipt is not accepted, and the reviewer asks for the itemised receipt (C8.2).

Team meals and conferences use the same reference as equipment, with the same 90-day validity. A reference is not needed for client entertainment, for office equipment up to EUR 300 per item, or for accessories up to EUR 50 per claim.
**IT3.6 Using a reference in a claim.** The employee enters the reference in the pre-approval field when submitting the claim. If a reference is required and the field is empty, the reviewer asks the employee for it under Expense Policy clause 7.2. A reference that was issued after the purchase, or that had expired on the purchase date, does not meet the requirement.
## 4. Home-office equipment
**IT4.1 What employees may buy.** Employees may buy monitors, keyboards, headsets and chairs themselves and claim them under the Expense Policy. Employees who prefer IT-supplied items can still request them in the portal at no cost. For other office items, such as a desk or a webcam, the employee asks IT first, because Finance assesses them under clause 4.1 of the Expense Policy.
**IT4.2 Limit of EUR 300 per item.** An item up to EUR 300 is reimbursed without a pre-approval reference (Expense Policy clause 4.1). The limit applies to each item and not to the whole order, so a EUR 250 monitor and a EUR 120 keyboard bought together are two items within the limit. The price counts after any discount and includes tax.

## 2. Requesting additional equipment through the IT portal
**IT2.1 The IT portal.** All requests for equipment that is not part of the standard kit are made in the IT portal, under "Request equipment". The request states what is needed, why, and the delivery address. Requests sent by email or chat are not tracked and are answered with a link to the portal.
**IT2.2 Approval.** The employee's manager approves the business need in the portal. IT then checks stock and either allocates a device from stock or orders a new one. IT does not approve a request that the manager has not approved.
**IT2.3 Delivery times.** IT delivers items it has in stock within 5 working days of the manager's approval. Items that IT must order are delivered within 15 working days. If an item is urgent, the request says so and the manager adds the reason; IT does not guarantee a shorter time, but it will say what is possible.
**IT2.4 Accessories.** IT keeps common cables, adapters and chargers in stock, and employees may request them in the portal at no cost. An employee may instead buy a small accessory personally. The Expense Policy (clause 4.3) reimburses accessories up to EUR 50 per claim, and a claim above that amount is rejected as a whole under Expense Policy clause 7.1.
**IT2.5 Laptops and phones are not bought personally.** IT supplies laptops and phones, and employees do not buy them. If an employee buys one personally, Finance can reimburse it only when a pre-approval reference was issued before the purchase, at any price (Expense Policy clause 4.1).

The trial uses the employee's work email address, never a personal card, and never customer data or production data. If the team wants to keep the tool, the manager requests a licence before the trial ends, because a trial that converts to a paid plan without IT is a personal purchase.
**IT5.4 Open-source tools.** IT keeps a list of approved open-source tools that employees may install without a request. For a tool that is not on the list, the employee raises a request, and IT checks the licence terms, how active the maintainers are, and known security problems. Free software is still software for the purposes of this policy, and a tool is not exempt from review because it costs nothing.
**IT5.5 Cancelling licences.** The manager reviews the licences of the team every quarter, and IT cancels the ones nobody uses. When an employee leaves, IT removes their licences on the last working day. A licence cannot be moved to a personal account.
## 6. Security requirements for any device used for work
**IT6.1 Device protection.** Every device used for work must have full-disk encryption on, a screen lock that starts after at most 5 minutes of inactivity, and the endpoint protection agent that IT installed. Employees do not turn off or remove these controls. USB storage devices are blocked on Larkfield laptops unless IT gives an exception.
**IT6.2 Accounts and passwords.** Work accounts use multi-factor authentication. Employees store passwords in the company password manager and never reuse a work password elsewhere. Passwords are not shared, written down or sent by email or chat, and a suspected leak is reported under clause IT7.1.
**IT6.3 Personal devices.** A personal phone or computer may be used for email, chat and the authentication app only after IT has enrolled it in device management. IT can remove work data from an enrolled personal device, but it cannot see personal data.

**FAQ-35. I am away for two weeks. Can I send my shirts to the hotel laundry?**
Yes, but only on trips of 5 nights or longer. On a shorter trip, laundry is a personal expense. Minibar, in-room entertainment and spa stay personal on any trip, however long. (Expense Policy 3.6)
## Equipment and software
**FAQ-36. Can I buy a monitor or a better chair myself and claim it?**
Office equipment such as monitors, keyboards, headsets and chairs is reimbursed up to EUR 300 per item without pre-approval. An item above EUR 300 needs a pre-approval reference from Finance before you buy it. (Expense Policy 4.1)
**FAQ-37. Can I buy a new laptop or phone myself?**
Laptops and phones are supplied by IT. If you buy one yourself, it needs a pre-approval reference at any price. Get the reference from Finance before the purchase. IT supplies the device, so ask IT first. (Expense Policy 4.1)
**FAQ-38. I paid for a software subscription that I use for work. Can I claim it?**
No. Software and subscriptions are bought by IT through the company account, so licences can be managed and cancelled. Software bought personally is not reimbursed, even when you use it for work. If you need a tool, ask IT to buy it. (Expense Policy 4.2)
**FAQ-39. What about a cable, an adapter or a phone case?**
Small accessories such as cables, adapters and phone cases are reimbursed up to EUR 50 per claim. Anything above EUR 50 in a single claim exceeds the limit, and the claim is rejected as a whole. (Expense Policy 4.3, 7.1)

**IT4.3 Items above EUR 300.** An item above EUR 300 needs a pre-approval reference issued before the purchase. The employee requests it as described in section 3 and attaches the product page or quote. If the employee buys such an item without a reference, Finance cannot reimburse it.
**IT4.4 Receipts.** The claim needs the itemised receipt or invoice required by Expense Policy clause 1.3. The business purpose says what the item is used for, for example "second monitor for home office". The employee submits the claim within 60 days of the document date.
**IT4.5 Ownership.** Items reimbursed under this section become the property of Larkfield. IT lists them in the IT portal under "My equipment" so that they can be found and returned. At the end of employment IT normally allows the employee to keep a chair, and requests monitors, keyboards and headsets back under section 8.
## 5. Software and subscriptions
**IT5.1 Software is bought through IT.** Software, cloud services, browser extensions and subscriptions used for work are requested in the IT portal and bought by IT through the company account (Expense Policy clause 4.2). IT assigns a licence to the employee's work account. The employee does not enter a payment card.
**IT5.2 Why personal purchases are not reimbursed.** Software bought personally is not reimbursed, even when it is used for work (Expense Policy clause 4.2). IT cannot see, renew, move or cancel a personal licence, and it cannot check the vendor's data protection terms. A subscription that nobody at Larkfield owns also continues to charge after the employee leaves.
**IT5.3 Free trials.** An employee may use a free trial for up to 30 days to test whether a tool is suitable, but only after telling IT in the portal.

Gift cards, vouchers and prepaid cards are not reimbursed, because they cannot be matched to a business expense. If you bought something real with the voucher, the policy does not cover that purchase through the voucher, so ask Finance. (Expense Policy 6.3)
**FAQ-46. I forgot my toothbrush and a clean shirt for the trip. Can I claim what I bought?**
No. Clothing and toiletries are personal expenses, even when you buy them on a business trip. (Expense Policy 6.2)
**FAQ-47. I earned airline miles on a business flight. Do I have to give them back?**
No. Points and miles earned on business expenses belong to you. Their value is neither reimbursed nor deducted. Your claim is for the money you spent, and the points you earned do not reduce it. (Expense Policy 6.4)
## Decisions and appeals
**FAQ-48. My claim says "needs info". What does that mean?**
The reviewer is missing something you can provide, such as the attendee list, the business purpose, a pre-approval reference or an itemised receipt. If the document could not be read, the reviewer asks for a new photo or file. It is not a rejection. The claim continues once you answer. (Expense Policy 7.2, 7.3)
**FAQ-49. My claim was rejected because it was over a limit. What now?**
Submit it again with the amount within the limit, and explain the difference in the business purpose. For example, a EUR 52 dinner on a trip is over the EUR 45 dinner limit and is rejected, while a claim for EUR 45 with a note is accepted. The policy describes no separate appeal. If you think the decision was wrong, ask Finance. The policy does not say that a new submission restarts the 60-day deadline, so do not wait.

## 0. Definitions
**0.1 Employee.** Anyone on the Larkfield payroll, including probation.
**0.2 Claim.** One uploaded receipt or invoice together with the information the employee enters when submitting it (business purpose, attendees, pre-approval reference).
**0.3 Business trip.** Travel more than 50 km from the employee's usual office, approved by the employee's manager.
**0.4 High-cost city.** London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York, Oslo.
**0.5 Pre-approval reference.** An identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN` issued by Finance before the purchase.
**0.6 Reviewer.** A member of the Finance team who makes the final decision on a claim.
**0.7 Currency.** All amounts are in euros (EUR). Where a receipt is in another currency, Finance converts it at the European Central Bank rate on the document date; limits apply to the converted amount.
## 1. General rules
**1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. An expense is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose.
**1.2 Submission deadline.** A claim must be submitted within 60 days of the document date. Claims submitted later are rejected. The deadline exists because Finance closes each quarter's accounts and late claims cannot be booked to the right period.
**1.3 Receipt requirements.** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice that shows the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, the total, and the tax amount where tax was charged. A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. Above EUR 25 the employee must provide the itemised receipt.
**1.4 Duplicates.** The same expense may be claimed only once.

## Submitting a claim
**FAQ-1. How do I get back money I paid out of my own pocket for work?**
Submit a claim with the receipt and one sentence saying what the spend was for. Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job, and "employee" includes anyone on the payroll, even during probation. A cost is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5)
**FAQ-2. Is it enough to write "work stuff" as the reason for the expense?**
No. Write one sentence that says what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" on its own is not accepted as a business purpose. A good example is "Dinner with the client team during the Hamburg trip", because a reviewer can read it and know what the money bought. (Expense Policy 1.5)
**FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?**
You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2)
**FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?**
Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2)
**FAQ-5. I uploaded the same receipt twice by mistake.

The business purpose states which of the two applies. A change made for the contractor's own convenience is a personal expense, and the cost is not reimbursed.
**C3.9 Parking and tolls.** Parking fees and road tolls paid during a business trip are reimbursed at their actual cost when the contractor attaches the receipt. They are claimed in addition to mileage under clause C3.4, because the mileage rate does not cover them. A parking ticket issued for an offence is a fine and is never reimbursed under clause C6.1.
## 4. Equipment and software
**C4.1 Equipment.** Equipment is never reimbursed to contractors. This covers monitors, keyboards, headsets, chairs, laptops and phones. Contractors supply their own equipment, and its cost is part of their fees. Where Larkfield needs a contractor to use Larkfield equipment, Larkfield supplies it directly through the engagement manager.
**C4.2 Software.** Software and subscriptions are never reimbursed to contractors, even when they are used only for the engagement. Where the engagement needs a Larkfield system, IT gives the contractor access to it, so that licences stay on the company account and can be cancelled when the engagement ends.
**C4.3 Accessories.** Accessories such as cables, adapters and phone cases are never reimbursed to contractors. The rule has no minimum amount, because small items are part of the contractor's own working costs.
## 5. Training and conferences
**C5.1 Books and courses.** Books, online courses and certification exams are not reimbursed to contractors, unless the statement of work says so. A statement of work that allows training names the amount or the course. Without that wording, the cost is the contractor's own investment in their skills.
**C5.2 Conferences.** Conference tickets are not reimbursed to contractors, unless the statement of work says so.

Is that a problem?**
The same expense may be claimed only once. Two claims with the same vendor, the same total and the same document date are treated as duplicates, and the later claim is rejected. Your first claim is not affected by this. You do not need to do anything about the first one. (Expense Policy 1.4)
**FAQ-6. I really did buy two identical things at the same shop on the same day. Will the system think I cheated?**
Two claims with the same vendor, total and document date look like duplicates, and the later one is rejected. If the two purchases were genuine, say so in the business purpose of the claim. That explanation is how the reviewer can tell the two claims apart. (Expense Policy 1.4)
**FAQ-7. I am not sure whether something is allowed. Who do I ask?**
Ask Finance, which owns the policy. Ask before you buy, because a pre-approval reference is issued before the purchase, and the policy has no way to get one afterwards. If the policy is silent on your situation, Finance is the team that answers. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1)
## Receipts
**FAQ-8. I lost the receipt. Can I still claim?**
Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice, and the policy has no rule that replaces a lost one. If you still have the payment card slip and the amount is EUR 25 or less, the slip is accepted. Above EUR 25 you must provide the itemised receipt. The policy does not say whether a bank or card statement can stand in, so ask Finance before you submit. (Expense Policy 1.3)
**FAQ-9. The shop only gave me the slip from the card machine. Is that enough?**
A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25.

For anything above EUR 25 you need the itemised receipt or invoice. If the shop can print or email an itemised copy, ask for it at the till, because it is the safer document to upload. (Expense Policy 1.3)
**FAQ-10. What does a receipt actually have to show?**
It must show the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, and the total. If tax was charged, the tax amount must be shown too. A receipt that shows only a total is not enough, except for the card slip case up to EUR 25. Check for these details before you leave the shop or close the booking page. (Expense Policy 1.3)
**FAQ-11. My receipt is in pounds. What amount do I claim?**
Claims are in euros, and Finance does the conversion for you. Finance converts at the European Central Bank rate on the document date. The limits in the policy apply to the converted amount, so check your spend against the limit in euros. (Expense Policy Definitions)
**FAQ-12. Finance sent my photo back because they could not read it. What now?**
When a document is blurred, cut off or missing the total, the reviewer asks you for a new photo or file instead of rejecting the claim. Upload a clear copy that shows the whole receipt, including the total. Lay the receipt flat in good light, and make sure the edges are inside the picture. (Expense Policy 7.3)
## Meals and entertainment
**FAQ-13. Can I grab a bite while I am away on a work trip, and how much can I spend?**
Yes, during a business trip. A business trip is travel more than 50 km from your usual office, approved by your manager. Meals are reimbursed at actual cost up to EUR 15 for breakfast, EUR 25 for lunch and EUR 45 for dinner. These limits apply to your own meal only.

If an item is urgent, the request says so and the manager adds the reason; IT does not guarantee a shorter time, but it will say what is possible.
**IT2.4 Accessories.** IT keeps common cables, adapters and chargers in stock, and employees may request them in the portal at no cost. An employee may instead buy a small accessory personally. **IT7.4 Replacement.** IT replaces a lost, stolen or irreparably damaged device from stock, or orders a new one, after the manager confirms the circumstances. A replacement does not restart the replacement cycle in clause IT1.6, so a laptop that is lost in its second year is replaced and is still due for renewal in year 3 of the original issue. Larkfield does not deduct the cost of a device from salary.
## 8. Returning equipment when leaving
**IT8.1 Return deadline.** The employee returns all Larkfield equipment within 14 days of the last working day. IT sends a prepaid courier box and a return label to remote employees. The employee should not wait for the box if they can return the equipment to an office.
**IT8.2 What is returned.** The employee returns the laptop, the phone, the headset, the chargers and any item reimbursed under section 4, apart from the items that IT releases to the employee. The employee also returns access cards, security keys and the original packaging if they still have it. IT checks the items against the list in the IT portal under "My equipment".
**IT8.3 Data and accounts.** Before returning a device, the employee copies any personal files to a personal storage and does not delete work files. IT disables the work accounts on the last working day and wipes the returned devices afterwards. Personal data left on a returned device is not recovered after the wipe.
**IT8.4 Equipment not returned.** If equipment has not arrived 30 days after the last working day, IT informs HR and Finance. Larkfield may recover the replacement value of the missing items as the employment contract and local law allow. Items that arrive later are accepted and the recovery is cancelled.

**FAQ-50. Can Finance just pay the part that is within the limit?**
No. Finance does not part-approve claims, so that every booked amount matches a document. A claim over a limit is rejected as a whole, and you submit it again with the amount within the limit. (Expense Policy 7.1)
**FAQ-51. My receipt has a few personal items mixed in with the work ones. What happens?**
The claim is rejected, and you submit it again without the personal items. Finance does not part-approve claims. (Expense Policy 7.4, 7.1)
**FAQ-52. How long does Finance take to review a claim?**
Finance aims for 5 working days. The policy itself sets no review time. If the reviewer asks you for information, the claim continues once you answer, so a quick answer keeps it moving. (Expense Policy 7.2)
## Using the intake desk
**FAQ-53. What do I have to fill in when I upload a receipt?**
A claim is one uploaded receipt or invoice plus the information you enter. Always enter the business purpose. Add the attendee list for client entertainment, and the pre-approval reference where the policy requires one: team meals, equipment above EUR 300, laptops and phones, and conference tickets. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.5, 2.2, 2.4, 4.1, 5.2)
**FAQ-54. Can I upload several receipts from one trip as a single claim?**
A claim is one receipt or invoice with its information, so each receipt is its own claim. The policy does not describe bundling several receipts into one upload, so ask Finance if you want to try. Each claim states its own business purpose, which is also what separates genuine look-alike purchases from duplicates.

## Submitting a claim
**FAQ-1. How do I get back money I paid out of my own pocket for work?**
Submit a claim with the receipt and one sentence saying what the spend was for. Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job, and "employee" includes anyone on the payroll, even during probation. A cost is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose. (Expense Policy Definitions, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5)
**FAQ-2. Is it enough to write "work stuff" as the reason for the expense?**
No. Write one sentence that says what the expense was for and which project, client or trip it belongs to. "Work" or "business" on its own is not accepted as a business purpose. A good example is "Dinner with the client team during the Hamburg trip", because a reviewer can read it and know what the money bought. (Expense Policy 1.5)
**FAQ-3. How long do I have to file a claim?**
You have 60 days from the date printed on the receipt or invoice (the document date). Claims submitted later are rejected. The count starts at the date on the document, not the date you got home. The reason is that Finance closes each quarter's accounts, and a late claim cannot be booked to the right period. (Expense Policy 1.2)
**FAQ-4. I found a receipt from three months ago. Can I still send it in?**
Three months is longer than 60 days, so the claim would be rejected. The policy lists no exceptions to the deadline. If you think your case has a special reason, ask Finance before you submit rather than assuming it will be accepted. (Expense Policy 1.2)

**FAQ-55. Who decides whether my claim is approved?**
A reviewer, who is a member of the Finance team, makes the final decision on a claim. The reviewer applies the Expense Policy, and where this FAQ differs from the policy, the policy decides. (Expense Policy Definitions, 7.1)

**IT7.1 Report within 24 hours.** An employee reports a lost or stolen device, or a suspected leak of credentials, to IT within 24 hours of noticing it. **IT7.2 What IT does.** On receiving the report IT locks the device and revokes its sessions, and it wipes the device if it is not recovered within 48 hours. **IT7.3 Damage.** The employee reports damage in the IT portal with a short description and, where possible, a photo. IT repairs the device or replaces it from stock. **IT7.4 Replacement.** IT replaces a lost, stolen or irreparably damaged device from stock, or orders a new one, after the manager confirms the circumstances. A replacement does not restart the replacement cycle in clause IT1.6, so a laptop that is lost in its second year is replaced and is still due for renewal in year 3 of the original issue. Larkfield does not deduct the cost of a device from salary.

**IT8.1 Return deadline.** The employee returns all Larkfield equipment within 14 days of the last working day. IT sends a prepaid courier box and a return label to remote employees. The employee should not wait for the box if they can return the equipment to an office.
**IT8.2 What is returned.** The employee returns the laptop, the phone, the headset, the chargers and any item reimbursed under section 4, apart from the items that IT releases to the employee. The employee also returns access cards, security keys and the original packaging if they still have it. IT checks the items against the list in the IT portal under "My equipment".
**IT8.3 Data and accounts.** Before returning a device, the employee copies any personal files to a personal storage and does not delete work files. IT disables the work accounts on the last working day and wipes the returned devices afterwards. Personal data left on a returned device is not recovered after the wipe.
**IT8.4 Equipment not returned.** If equipment has not arrived 30 days after the last working day, IT informs HR and Finance. Larkfield may recover the replacement value of the missing items as the employment contract and local law allow. Items that arrive later are accepted and the recovery is cancelled.

## 0. Definitions
**0.1 Employee.** Anyone on the Larkfield payroll, including probation.
**0.2 Claim.** One uploaded receipt or invoice together with the information the employee enters when submitting it (business purpose, attendees, pre-approval reference).
**0.3 Business trip.** Travel more than 50 km from the employee's usual office, approved by the employee's manager.
**0.4 High-cost city.** London, Paris, Zurich, Geneva, New York, Oslo.
**0.5 Pre-approval reference.** An identifier of the form `PA-YYYY-NNN` issued by Finance before the purchase.
**0.6 Reviewer.** A member of the Finance team who makes the final decision on a claim.
**0.7 Currency.** All amounts are in euros (EUR). Where a receipt is in another currency, Finance converts it at the European Central Bank rate on the document date; limits apply to the converted amount.
## 1. General rules
**1.1 Purpose.** Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job. An expense is reasonable when a colleague in the same role would have spent a similar amount for the same business purpose.
**1.2 Submission deadline.** A claim must be submitted within 60 days of the document date. Claims submitted later are rejected. The deadline exists because Finance closes each quarter's accounts and late claims cannot be booked to the right period.
**1.3 Receipt requirements.** Every claim needs an itemised receipt or invoice that shows the vendor name, the document date, each item purchased, the total, and the tax amount where tax was charged. A payment card slip that shows only a total is accepted for amounts up to EUR 25. Above EUR 25 the employee must provide the itemised receipt.
**1.4 Duplicates.** The same expense may be claimed only once.

The reviewer is missing something you can provide, such as the attendee list, the business purpose, a pre-approval reference or an itemised receipt. **FAQ-49. My claim was rejected because it was over a limit. What now?**
Submit it again with the amount within the limit, and explain the difference in the business purpose. For example, a EUR 52 dinner on a trip is over the EUR 45 dinner limit and is rejected, while a claim for EUR 45 with a note is accepted. The policy describes no separate appeal. Costs of the contractor's own staff or subcontractors are reimbursed only when the statement of work names them, and they are bound by the same limits. Larkfield cannot check expenses of people it has no agreement with, so an unnamed subcontractor's receipts are rejected.

Expenses incurred before that day, while the contractor was engaged under a statement of work, stay under this policy and go on the last contractor invoice. Keeping the two periods apart means each expense is judged by the limits that applied when it was incurred.
## 2. Meals
**C2.1 Meals during business trips.** During a business trip, Larkfield reimburses meals at their actual cost up to these limits per meal: breakfast EUR 12, lunch EUR 20, dinner EUR 35. **C2.2 Client entertainment.** A meal with Larkfield clients is reimbursed only when the engagement manager approved it in writing before the meal.
